HSBC reported H1 2026 revenue of $38.2 billion, up 6% YoY, and PBT of $20.4 billion, up 6%, with an annualized RoTE of 19.1%, above the 17% target. Banking NII guidance was raised to at least $46 billion for the full year. CET1 ratio was 14.1%, and the company announced a $1 billion share buyback, resuming after a pause. Cost of risk was 47bps for H1, with Q2 HK CRE charges of $0.2 billion; full-year guidance of 45bps was reiterated.

Entegris reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $883 million, up 11% year-over-year and above guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.93, up 42%. Gross margin was 47.6%, its highest since early 2022, and free cash flow was $120 million. The company raised its 2026 MSI growth outlook to 7-8% from mid-single digits, guided Q3 revenue to $905-935 million (up ~14% YoY), and expects to end the year with net leverage below 3x. It also announced the exit of its Life Sciences Fluid Management business and further facility rationalization.

Enlight Renewable Energy reported Q2 2026 revenue and income of $210 million, up 55% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $160 million, up 67%. Net profit reached $31 million. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $790-820 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $565-585 million. Key milestones include financial close on the $2.6 billion CO Bar Complex, a PPA with Google for 200 MW in Oklahoma, and safe harboring 17.9 FGW of capacity.

Custom Truck One Source reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $563M, up 10% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $117M, up 25% YoY. SER revenue grew 20% to $219M with utilization up 400 bps to 81.6%, and STEM third-party revenue hit a record $345M. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.1B-$2.2B and adjusted EBITDA to $437.5M-$455M, citing a 'transmission demand super cycle' and strong order flow. Net leverage improved to 3.85x, and management expects meaningful free cash flow generation in 2026.

Centerspace reported Q2 FY2026 Core FFO of $1.27 per share with same-store NOI up 30 basis points year-over-year. The company sold or contracted to watch 20 communities for ~$530 million over 14 months, reducing leverage and exiting tertiary markets. Due to the reconstituted same-store pool, full-year same-store NOI growth guidance was lowered to flat to down 1%, and Core FFO midpoint lowered to $4.63 per share. Management remains confident in the portfolio repositioning, expects Denver to recover in 2027, and anticipates a special distribution in Q4 to maintain REIT status.

Crescent Energy reported record Q2 2026 results with production of 335 Mboe/d (2% above guidance midpoint), oil production 4% above midpoint, and record levered free cash flow of $418 million. Adjusted EBITDAX was $798 million. The company raised full-year production guidance and improved opex guidance, while maintaining capex. Permian synergies were increased to $250-$300 million, roughly three times the original target, and the company sees continued upside.

Q2 FY2026 revenue of $213M grew 53% YoY, beating guidance of $200-202M; operating income of $62M doubled YoY with 29% margin (up from 19%), and free cash flow reached $100M (47% margin). LTM billings hit $862M, up 52%. The company raised guidance on yield-driven strength and announced a definitive agreement to acquire Cylinder Health for $105M cash to enter GI, plus a $300M share buyback. Management cited strong pipeline, SMB growth, and rapid adoption of the new Migraine program.

Danaos reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net income of $133.1 million ($7.29 per share), up from $117 million ($6.36 per share) year-over-year, driven by a strong dry bulk segment where adjusted EBITDA jumped from $5.9M to $18.8M. Backlog increased by $683 million to a record $4.6 billion, with 100% container coverage for 2026, 93% for 2027, and 61% for 2029. Net debt was low at $224.5 million (0.3x EBITDA), cash stood at $1 billion, and fleet remains 78 of 87 vessels debt-free. Management expressed caution on new investments at elevated prices and expects FID for Alaska LNG around September.

Horizon Quantum reported Q2 2026 net loss of $115.2 million, driven mainly by a $108.3 million non-cash warrant derivative remeasurement charge. Operating expenses rose to $7.2 million from $2.8 million a year ago, reflecting increased R&D and public company costs. Cash reached $113.3 million, boosted by $27.5 million in warrant exercise proceeds. Key progress includes Beryllium early access, Ember-1 testbed opening to users, and a new internal applications team, while management notes a large non-cash loss that does not affect runway.

DuPont reported Q2 FY2026 organic sales growth of 4%, operating EBITDA margin up 80 basis points to 24.6%, adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.88, and free cash flow conversion of 127% for the quarter. The company raised full-year guidance again: organic growth to slightly ahead of 4%, operating EBITDA midpoint to $1.760B, and adjusted EPS midpoint to $7.24 (up $0.15). Management also announced a Q3 $250M share repurchase and expects full-year free cash flow conversion ahead of the 90% target. Strength was driven by healthcare, aerospace, industrial water, semiconductor, and electric vehicle battery applications, with continued momentum expected in the second half.

Ecopetrol reported strong Q2 2026 results with revenue up 35% YoY to COP 40.2 trillion, EBITDA up 59% to COP 17.7 trillion, and net income up 235% to COP 6.1 trillion, driven by higher Brent prices and record refining throughput. Management highlighted improved crude differentials, record refining margins, and continued investment progress, while noting production impacts from external disruptions and a higher FEPC receivable. The company expects to consolidate Brava Energia results in Q3 2026 and reaffirmed its dividend commitment.

Ingredion's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 1% to $1.85 billion, in line with expectations, but adjusted operating income fell 5% to $258 million and adjusted EPS declined $0.05 due to Argo production issues and Mexico macro pressures. Texture & Healthful Solutions delivered 7% volume growth (ninth consecutive quarter) and its second-highest quarterly operating income, but tapioca costs rose over 40% year-to-date. U.S./CAN sales fell 7% and operating income was $58 million; management expects sequential improvement in the back half from Argo recovery. The pending Tate & Lyle acquisition received shareholder approval, with expected EPS accretion above 15% in the first full year.

IIPR reported Q2 2026 revenue of $63.3 million, down from $69 million in Q1, with AFFO per share of $1.83 versus $1.88, due to reduced payments from default tenants. The company fully funded its $270 million IQHQ commitment, completed an upsized $402.5 million exchangeable notes offering at 6%, and repaid its $291 million senior debt maturity, ending with $300 million liquidity and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 1.7x. Leasing activity included 389,000 sq ft of new leases in H1, plus 488,000 sq ft of agreements on former 4Front assets, while Parallel defaulted on two Florida properties totaling 593,000 sq ft. Management expressed confidence in life sciences diversification and federal cannabis reform progress.

Crexendo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.6 million, up 49% year-over-year, beating top-line expectations, with GAAP net income of $1.1 million ($0.03 per share) in line with expectations and non-GAAP net income of $4.1 million ($0.12 per share), beating expectations by 200 basis points. Adjusted EBITDA of $4.1 million was up 46% year-over-year, and margins expanded across all segments, with consolidated gross margin up 500 basis points sequentially to 66%. The company added six new NetSapiens logos in the quarter (11 year-to-date vs. 2 last year), ESI acquisition contributed $6.9 million in revenue, and remaining performance obligation increased 97% to $139 million. Management maintained double-digit organic growth guidance for the year and expects AI-related revenue to become meaningful in 2027.

3D Systems reported Q2 FY2026 with printer sales up over 45% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for new platforms like DMP 350, SLA 825, and NextDent 300. Healthcare remained the largest segment with solid growth, while industrial revenue was modestly lower due to older system replacements, but aerospace/defense and data center infrastructure both grew double digits. The company announced a leadership transition and signed a CRADA with Savannah River National Laboratory for nuclear materials. Guidance implies a small EBITDA loss in Q3, with management confident in reaching positive EBITDA through volume growth and material pull-through.

IDEXX reported Q2 2026 revenue up 10% as reported and 9% organically, with CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growing 10.3% organically, led by double-digit volume growth in both U.S. and international. EPS was $4.27, up 15% on a comparable basis, with comparable operating margin up 110 basis points. Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, citing strong performance and momentum, while noting headwinds from FX and planned incremental investments in the second half.

Chatham Lodging Trust reported a strong Q2 2026, with RevPAR up 3%, pro forma GOP margins up 170 basis points, and hotel EBITDA margins up 220 basis points, beating internal expectations. The company increased its annual guidance by approximately 20% since the start of the year, citing strong business travel, robust performance from the recently acquired six-hotel portfolio (RevPAR up 9% in Q2 and 13% in July), and accelerating Silicon Valley demand (July RevPAR up 26%). Management remains optimistic about the lodging upcycle but exercises conservatism in second-half guidance due to Middle East conflict and limited visibility.

DigitalOcean reported Q2 2026 revenue of $281 million, up 29% YoY, exceeding guidance on all key metrics. The company raised its full year 2026 revenue growth outlook to approximately 30% and reaffirmed at least 35% growth by Q4 2026, while expressing heightened confidence in 50%+ growth for 2027. Inference services grew nearly 800% YoY and now represent over 70% of AI customer ARR, with over 6,000 Inference Engine customers. Management highlighted strong profitability with 40% adjusted EBITDA margin and record incremental ARR of $93 million in the quarter.

Dorman reported record Q2 2026 sales of $545 million, up ~1% YoY, and record adjusted EPS of $3.08, up 50% YoY, with a $1.18 one-time refund benefit from IEEPA tariff costs. Excluding that benefit, comparable EPS was $1.90. Light Duty sales were flat YoY on tough comps, Heavy Duty grew ~7%, Specialty Vehicle declined 1%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3%-5% net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $8.50-$8.80, reflecting lower tariff environment and pricing actions. Heavy Duty margin improved 150 bps ex-refund, but freight market remains challenged.

Hut 8 reported Q2 FY2026 results, emphasizing its energy infrastructure platform and progress on AI data center campuses. The company announced a second Beacon Point lease for 352 MW, bringing total contracted AI data center capacity to about 949 MW with roughly $26.6 billion of expected base term contract value. Construction milestones at River Bend are on track, and the company highlighted two investment-grade construction financings, with Beacon Point on better terms. Management remains confident in delivery and cost efficiency, noting building costs are declining per building.

Duke Energy reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.43, up from $1.25 in the prior year, driven by electric utility growth and infrastructure investments. The company reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $6.55-$6.80 and its 5%-7% growth through 2030, expressing confidence in top-half results from 2028. Management highlighted a favorable North Carolina rate settlement, 7.8 GW of data center ESAs, and $5B-$10B of potential capital-plan upside.

Harmony Biosciences reported record Q2 2026 WAKIX net revenue of $261.3 million, up 30% year-over-year and 21% sequentially, and reiterated full-year guidance of $1.0-$1.04 billion, on track to exceed $1 billion. The company disclosed encouraging phase I SAD data for BP-205, an orexin-2 agonist, showing a 25-hour half-life, once-daily dosing potential, and no serious adverse events, with MAD data expected in Q4 and phase II trials planned for mid-2027. Management emphasized strong balance sheet with ~$963 million cash and IP protection for WAKIX to 2030.

HealthStream reported record Q2 FY2026 revenues of $83.7 million, up 12.5% YoY, and record adjusted EBITDA of $20.6 million, up 16.9%. Organic growth was 8.3%, with notable strength in CredentialStream (+14%), ShiftWizard (+30%), and myClinicalExchange (+29%). The company raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance but trimmed net income guidance due to planned incremental investments in career networks. A $2 million one-time revenue catch-up from an ANSOS contract contributed to results and is not recurring.

Coupang reported Q2 2026 product commerce revenue growth of 8% in constant currency, improving sequentially from 5% in Q1, with consolidated revenue up 10% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA came in within guidance, but product commerce gross margin contracted 210 bps YoY due to supply chain headwinds, promotional activity, and a $410 million regulatory fine. Membership recovered above pre-incident levels, and underlying customer spend (excluding non-returned cohort) grew 16% YoY, but management guided Q3 to 8-9% growth, citing calendar effects and the missing cohort. Management expects margin recovery for product commerce by mid-2027.

Compass reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.3 billion, up 14% year-over-year on a pro forma basis, and record adjusted EBITDA of $363 million, both above guidance. The company raised its year-one cost synergies target to $330 million from $300 million, achieved five months ahead of schedule, and increased 2026 in-year net synergies to $220 million. Brokerage GTV grew about 16% year-over-year versus market up 6%, an acceleration in outperformance from Q1, and net debt/EBITDA fell to 3.3x from 4.2x sequentially.

Cummins reported record Q2 sales of $9.5 billion, up 9% YoY, and record EBITDA of $1.7 billion (17.5% of sales), though EBITDA margin decreased from 18.4%. The company raised its full-year revenue growth guidance to 10%-13% (from 8%-11%) and increased EBITDA margin midpoint to 18%-18.5%. Strong demand in power generation, data centers, and China drove results, with global power generation revenue growth expected to remain 15%-25%, though capacity constraints persist.

Centuri delivered record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $962M, up 33% YoY, with adjusted net income up 44% to $24.4M. Base revenue grew 36% and base gross profit grew 21%, though base gross margin contracted to 7.9% from 8.9% due to fuel costs and capacity investments. The company raised full-year guidance, expecting revenue of $3.59-$3.79B and adjusted EBITDA of $285-$310M, including the JJ White acquisition. Backlog is up 21% to $6.4B and the pipeline grew to $16B, with data center demand a key driver.

Henry Schein reported strong Q2 2026 with accelerated internal local currency sales growth and margin expansion, driving double-digit earnings growth. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance, though EPS guidance was only modestly increased due to excluding further remeasurement gains. Management highlighted broad-based strength, with high-growth businesses now nearly 50% of operating income and continued momentum expected.

Grainger delivered strong Q2 FY2026 results with total sales up 10.3% reported and 13.7% on a daily organic constant currency basis, driven by broad-based demand acceleration. Operating margin expanded 120 bps to 16.1%, and EPS rose over 20% to $12.01, aided by IEEPA tariff refunds. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting daily organic constant currency sales growth of 11.5%-13% and EPS of $45.50-$47.25, with preliminary July sales up over 13%.

FIS reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.4 billion, up 5.3% pro forma, with banking growing 6.1% at the high end of guidance and capital markets growing 3.2% at the low end. Adjusted EBITDA grew 7.4% with 113bps margin expansion, adjusted EPS up 8.8%, and free cash flow more than tripled to $525 million, leading to a $100 million raise in full-year free cash flow guidance. However, capital markets underperformed due to client attrition from UBS/Credit Suisse and weaker lending volumes, prompting a rebased full-year outlook and a review of strategic alternatives for some capital markets products.

Gilead reported strong Q2 2026 results with base business sales up 10% YoY, driven by HIV, Trodelvy, and Livdelzi. HIV sales grew 12% YoY, with PrEP sales doubling to exceed $1 billion quarterly for the first time. The company raised full-year HIV growth guidance to 9%-10% from 8%, citing strong Biktarvy and PrEP momentum. Trodelvy sales were up 26% YoY on new first-line approvals, while cell therapy declined 14% YoY amid competition. Management highlighted upcoming launches for BIC/LEN and anito-cel before year-end.

Fortune Brands Innovations reported Q2 2026 sales of $1.2 billion, down 4%, with operating income up 18.4% to $236 million and EPS of $1.35, both benefiting from $81 million net tariff refunds ($0.52 EPS). Excluding tariff refunds, results were in line with expectations; Water sales fell 6.5% due to service challenges and supply chain issues, while Outdoors and Security showed some growth. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance to fund incremental investments of about $0.20 EPS for service and new product development, and reaffirmed a $70 million cost program with $15 million savings in 2026. The tone was realistic and candid, acknowledging execution gaps and emphasizing a return to customer focus.

Graphic Packaging reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $247 million at the top of guidance, adjusted EPS of $0.14, and adjusted cash flow of $138 million, up $55 million year-over-year. Margins expanded sequentially to 11.3%, with volumes steady despite higher gas prices. The company raised its 2026 inflation estimate to $150 million, achieved $85 million in cost savings, and reduced capital expenditure guidance to below $450 million, but lowered adjusted cash flow guidance to $600-$700 million due to inflation and inventory timing. Management announced price increases and progress on footprint optimization, but noted softness in household and foodservice segments.

In Q2 2026, Diamondback Energy increased production by ~4% from year-start, responding to price signals with a 3-4% hike in March. Management cited low global inventories and expects continued low single-digit organic growth in 2027 while maintaining capital efficiency. They reduced net debt by $1.6 billion, translating to $5.60 per share of value, and allocated modestly to buybacks. Gas outperformance and EOR results were highlighted, with initial EOR wells showing 100-150 bbl/d uplift on average, though dispersion is wide.

HLMN reported Q2 FY2026 net sales up 10% to $442M, in line with long-term growth targets, with adjusted EBITDA up 2.5% to $77.1M. The company announced the acquisition of Kanebridge Corporation for $315M, which is expected to add $15M in sales and $5M in adjusted EBITDA in 2026, and raised the midpoint of full-year net sales guidance to $1.695B (9% growth) and adjusted EBITDA to $285M. RDS segment showed strong growth with adjusted EBITDA up 10.4% and margins healthy. New business wins contributed 4.5 points of growth, including about 1 point from the Win the Pro focus, and the company remains confident in its long-term 8-12% growth target.

Global Industrial reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $386.6 million, with average daily sales up 9.3% YoY (third consecutive quarter of high single-digit ADS growth). Non-GAAP gross margin was 34.7% (more in line with historical performance, down from a record 37.1% that included FIFO tariff timing benefits), and non-GAAP operating margin was 7.3%. The quarter included a one-time $26 million benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds (excluded from non-GAAP). Management noted continued momentum into Q3, with GPO annualized sales on pace to hit $100 million and e-procurement connections now greater than 1,300. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management indicated gross margins should remain around 34.7%-34.8% for the balance of the year, and reiterated CapEx of $3-$4 million.

IPG Photonics reported Q2 2026 revenue of $279 million, up 11% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $0.58, both above expectations. Adjusted gross margin of 40.7% beat guidance, aided by a $4.7 million tariff refund and lower costs. Bookings improved with book-to-bill above one, led by strong welding and battery manufacturing demand. The company announced a binding offer to acquire Lumibird Medical and provided Q3 revenue guidance of $265-295 million with adjusted EPS of $0.30-0.60.

In Q2 2026, Gulfport highlighted strong momentum heading into the second half, with production accelerating and liquids volumes expected to be over 50% higher than H1. Management announced a $140 million discretionary land budget for 2026 and disclosed a recent $83 million state land auction purchase, boosting net Appalachia location count by ~20%. New CEO Nick Dell'Osso emphasized operational efficiency, inventory quality (about 15 years of drilling inventory with best-in-class breakevens), and disciplined capital allocation including buybacks. The company remains optimistic about in-basin gas demand from AI data centers and is exploring value in the Scoop asset. No specific financial figures were provided in the text.

The call did not provide specific reported financials for Q2 FY2026; instead, management discussed strategic plans. They mentioned a $1.2 billion MSA contract with a neocloud provider, targeting first 10 MW of critical load online by end of 2026 and next 10 MW in Q1 2027. Management presented a projection of $300 million-$350 million enterprise value next year and anticipates reporting EBITDA starting in 2027. They acknowledged ongoing dilution concerns and the need to raise capital, while planning to reduce corporate overhead.

IQM reported Q2 FY2026 with strong commercial traction: cumulative 26 full-stack quantum computers sold, 17 delivered, and eight in production. The company completed a dual listing on Nasdaq and expanded into new markets with enterprise sales and a LUMI contract worth EUR 33 million. Full-year order intake guidance is EUR 65-75 million, with a cautious but confident outlook, and cash runway extended to Q2 2028. Cloud revenue remains small but is expected to grow as applications mature.

Independence Realty Trust reported Q2 FY2026 core FFO per share of $0.28, ahead of internal expectations, with same-store NOI growth of 1.2% outpacing the original guidance midpoint. The company raised its full-year same-store NOI growth guidance midpoint by 70 basis points to 1.5%, but maintained core FFO per share guidance at $1.14 due to higher interest expense and lower non-same-store NOI. Management highlighted accelerating new lease spreads, a successful Wi-Fi initiative contributing $400,000 in Q2 revenue, and a commitment to value-add renovations as key drivers for 2027 momentum.

Q2 2026 revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million, slightly below guidance, and adjusted EPS of $0.34 was at the midpoint. Management highlighted an inflection point with over $30 million in significant new platform-led deals closed, expected to drive Q3 EPS of $0.37-$0.39 and a strong Q4 and 2027. Gross margin improved to 44.1% from 42.3% sequentially, and cash flow from operations was $15.2 million.

Flywire reported strong second quarter FY2026 results with robust revenue and EBITDA growth, signing over 200 new clients across 45 countries for the second consecutive quarter. Management emphasized strategic vendor consolidation, geographic diversification, and software-led monetization as structural growth drivers, with education revenue outside the big four growing over 30% year-over-year. The company reiterated long-term targets of $1 billion annual organic revenue and 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, while acknowledging a challenging macro environment with negative U.K. visa trends and stricter regulations. AI-driven automation is already resolving ~45% of customer inquiries automatically, with a target of over 50% by year-end.

First Watch reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue growth of 15.2% to $354.7 million, with same-restaurant sales up 3.4% and traffic nearly flat at -0.4% but improving sequentially. Restaurant-level operating profit margin improved 20 basis points to 18.8%, helped by commodity deflation and labor productivity, though beef costs pressured margin by ~100 basis points due to strong LTO demand. Management maintained FY2026 guidance and updated long-term targets to 50 annual openings and positive free cash flow by FY2027, while emphasizing marketing effectiveness and robust development pipeline.

EVERTEC reported Q2 2026 revenue of $275 million, up 20% year-over-year (16% on a constant currency basis), with adjusted EBITDA of $109 million (up 18%) and adjusted EPS of $1.05 (up 18%). The quarter included significant strategic wins, including a multi-year agreement with Transbank in Chile and a contract with Clip in Mexico, and the acquisitions of Dimensa and BBChain closed in the quarter. Management confirmed existing guidance and noted synergies from acquisitions are expected to be more meaningful in 2027.

FMS reported Q2 FY2026 with solid 5% organic revenue growth and 23% operating income growth at constant currency, plus 180 bps margin expansion. However, U.S. same-market treatment growth declined 0.9%, and management lowered expectations for 2026 U.S. same-market treatment growth to around Q2 levels due to referral execution gaps. The company confirmed full-year guidance, completed a EUR 1 billion buyback and launched a second, while absorbing external cost headwinds and regulatory pressures in China.

Innovex delivered Q2 2026 revenue of $245 million and adjusted EBITDA of $48 million, both at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 20%. International/offshore revenue rose 11% sequentially, while NAM land fell 4% sequentially due to Canada seasonality. The company closed the TCO Group acquisition for $95 million and guided Q3 revenue to $260-270 million and adjusted EBITDA to $51-57 million, implying sequential growth. Management cited strong subsea momentum, Mexico activity, Saudi market share gains, and expects U.S. land growth in the back half.

Finance of America reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $19 million ($0.84 per share), up 53% year-over-year, despite a GAAP net loss of $29 million driven by non-cash fair value adjustments. Funded reverse mortgages totaled $730 million, up 21% year-over-year, and submissions exceeded $1 billion, up 19% year-over-year. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of $2.8-3.1 billion in funded volume and $4.50-$5.00 adjusted EPS, and highlighted strong cash generation of $58 million in the quarter, used to fund the Onity MSR acquisition and debt payments. Management expressed confidence in achieving guidance and continued investment in growth.

Freshworks reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $237.4M, up 16% YoY, above the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP operating margin was 24%, and the company achieved positive GAAP net income of $3.2M ahead of schedule. EX ARR grew 24% constant currency to $567M, while CX ARR grew 4% to $400M. The company raised full-year guidance, citing a $4M beat inclusive of a $2M FX headwind, and reaffirmed confidence in mid-20s EX ARR growth.

Easterly reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $92.4 million, up 10% YoY, and Core FFO per share of $0.78, up from $0.74 YoY, above the long-term growth target. The company raised its full-year Core FFO guidance midpoint by $0.01 to $3.07-$3.13. Occupancy was 98% with a weighted average lease term of 9.2 years. Management expressed confidence in converting a $1.5 billion pipeline as the stock price improves, while maintaining a strong balance sheet with a new $200 million term loan.

Backblaze reported Q2 2026 revenue of $42.7 million, above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 30%, also above guidance. B2 growth accelerated to 34% year-over-year, and the company signed its largest contract ever, a $335 million multi-year agreement with CoreWeave. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $172-$174 million (from $161.5-$163.5 million) and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 27%-29% (from 23%-25%). B2 ARR reached $113 million, up 39% year-over-year, and the company provided early directional commentary of 40%+ B2 revenue growth in 2027.

Adeia reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $96.1 million, in line with expectations, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 59% and strong cash generation of $54.6 million. The company closed six license agreements and added a record 12 new customers, including a multi-year renewal with Google and a multi-year agreement with RPX covering 10 member companies. Management reiterated FY2026 revenue guidance of $395-$435 million and raised its long-term revenue target to $600 million from $500 million, driven by an increased semiconductor opportunity of $200 million (up from $100 million). Non-pay TV recurring revenue grew 54% year-over-year.

In Q2 FY2026, ABTC mined 932 Bitcoin, up 14% QoQ, with revenue of ~$67M, up 8% despite a 12% decline in Bitcoin price. Gross margin compressed to 49% from 52% due to price, though cost per Bitcoin stayed flat at ~$36,500. The strategic reserve grew 14% to 8,002 Bitcoin, and Satoshis per share rose 11% QoQ. Management remains confident, citing record production, stable costs, and continued reserve growth, while noting macro headwinds and a CFO transition.

Advanced Energy reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $574M, up 30% YoY and EPS of $2.74, up 83% YoY, both above the high end of guidance. Gross margin improved 380 bps YoY to 41.9%, and operating margin reached 21.9%, a multi-year high. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to low-to-mid 30% (from low-to-mid 20%), raised data center growth outlook to at least 50%, and guided Q3 revenue of ~$640M with EPS of $3.00. Management cited strength across all markets, with semiconductor sequential growth of 27% and record revenue in that segment.

CNH reported Q2 2026 consolidated revenues of $4.8 billion, up 2% YoY, with Ag sales up 1% and Construction up 12%. Adjusted EPS was $0.13, and adjusted EBIT margin for Ag fell to 5.2% from 8.1%, with Construction EBIT margin down to 1.7% from 4.5%. Management guided to flat net sales for 2026, moving to the high end of the previous range, and expects an L-shaped recovery with 2027 retail demand broadly flat. Tariffs were reduced on certain products, but remain a net drag, and the company is filing $135 million in phase II tariff refund claims.

SBA Communications reported Q2 2026 FFO per share of $3.05 and a dividend of $1.25 per share, while modestly raising full-year guidance for site leasing revenue, FFO, and FFO per share. The company issued $3.5 billion in investment-grade bonds, upgraded to BBB by S&P, and reduced leverage to 6.4x net debt to EBITDA. Management highlighted steady U.S. activity, international expansion, and longer-term opportunities from spectrum auctions, edge compute, and satellite terrestrial complements, while resuming share buybacks in the second half.

ClearPoint reported Q2 2026 revenue of $10.9 million, up 18% year-over-year, driven by Neurosurgery Navigation and Capital Equipment growth, while Biologics and Drug Delivery revenue fell 15% on a non-recurring prior-year order. Gross margin improved to 62%, but operating expenses rose sharply (S&M +68%, G&A +64%), and cash dropped to $29.4 million. Management adjusted 2026 revenue guidance down to $48-$52 million, citing a shift in investment toward clinical support, CAL (GLP lab), focused ultrasound robotics, and Harmony software, and highlighted multiple pharma partner regulatory advancements and the first GLP service contract at the new Torrey Pines facility.

Allison reported Q2 2026 net sales of $1.566 billion, up 92% YoY, with the Allison Transmission segment hitting a record $860 million and defense revenue up 57% YoY. The company raised its full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance, primarily due to stronger Allison Transmission outlook, and expects $120 million in annual synergies by 2029 with none material in 2026. Three major defense contract wins, including a landmark $250 million order for the 4040MX, underscore strong defense momentum and a full order board into 2027.

Ameresco delivered Q2 revenue of $515 million, up 9% YoY, with project revenue up 6% and energy asset revenue up 21%. Awarded project backlog surged 65% to a record $4.4 billion, including $1.8 billion in new awards driven by data centers ($1.2 billion) and other markets. The company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook and raised non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.15-$1.35 due to a higher expected tax benefit. Management expressed confidence in strong future growth from data center projects, with major revenue impact expected in 2028-2030.

BWXT reported strong Q2 results: revenue up 18% with 9% organic growth, adjusted EBITDA up 7%, and adjusted EPS up 5% to $1.7. Government operations saw margin expansion to 20.9% despite lower revenue growth, while commercial operations showed 72% total revenue growth and 33% organic growth. The company raised full-year free cash flow guidance and adjusted EBITDA guidance, but lowered government revenue growth outlook due to favorable cost performance. It closed the PCG acquisition, is evaluating further U.S. capacity expansion, and signed agreements to license mPower technology.

The call focused on wildfires near Spokane causing significant infrastructure damage, with 7,300 electric and 5,300 natural gas customers out of service. Management confirmed its facilities did not start the fires and highlighted effective wildfire mitigation measures. Financially, the quarter included non-regulated gains, notably from EIP's investment in ERock, with expected next-quarter gains likely to reverse. The Washington rate case is expected to be difficult to settle due to fundamental differences on the four-year plan term, with a hearing set for September 17-18.

SI-BONE reported Q2 2026 revenue of $56 million, up 15.2% globally and 14.7% in the U.S., with strong procedure volume growth and 178% improvement in adjusted EBITDA to $2.8 million. The company submitted a 510(k) for a third breakthrough device expected to launch as early as October, and pointed to proposed CMS reimbursement increases across outpatient settings and new DRGs for complex spine procedures as significant tailwinds. Management raised confidence in a strong finish to 2026 and sees additional momentum in 2027, while deliberately increasing R&D investment in the second half.

EchoStar's Q2 FY2026 call was dominated by Hughes filing Chapter 11 bankruptcy, with management confirming a $1.5 billion bond maturity triggered restructuring. Management reiterated a $5-7 billion expected total tax and network termination cost for the SpaceX deal, with cash at $14-15 billion and a $2.4 billion escrow set aside. They reported 'slightly cash positive' Boost Wireless but lost subscribers, and management admitted they 'haven't cracked the code' in wireless. The board increased buyback authorization to $5 billion, but management cited bond indenture restrictions and a preference for investing in the business before buybacks.

In Q2 FY2026, EverQuote grew revenue 25% year-over-year to $195.1 million and adjusted EBITDA 37% to a record $30.1 million, with a 15.4% margin. The home vertical grew 35% to $23 million, while auto revenue grew 23% to $172.1 million. Guidance for Q3 is $198-$208 million revenue and $28-$31 million adjusted EBITDA, representing 17% and 18% year-over-year growth at midpoints. Management reaffirmed its path to $1 billion annual revenue.

Vertex reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $204 million, up 10.5% year-over-year, at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA up 33% to $51 million (25% margin). However, management acknowledged slower cloud conversions and new logo activity, leading to a lower full-year cloud growth outlook (now ~18% for the year, down from previous expectations). E-invoicing momentum was strong with several six-figure deals and expectations for continued benefit from upcoming French and German mandates, but revenue impact is expected to be more back-half weighted. Retention metrics were stable at 95% gross and 105% net revenue retention.

Matson reported a strong second quarter: consolidated operating income was $158.9 million, up $45.9 million year over year, with diluted EPS up 46.2% to $4.27. China service volumes rose 15.2% with freight rates above expectations, driving the beat. Management raised full-year 2026 consolidated operating income guidance to exceed $499.8 million, and expects Q3 ocean transportation operating income to be about 45% higher than the prior year. Logistics operating income increased modestly, and the company continues to repurchase shares and return capital.

Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.6 billion, non-GAAP gross margin 39.3%, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 all exceeded the midpoint of guidance. AI data center revenue is now expected to more than double in 2026, and silicon carbide revenue in China is expected to grow 60-70% YoY. The company also announced plans to acquire Synaptics and continues to return capital, with Q2 free cash flow of $425 million and $332 million returned to shareholders.

Twist Bioscience reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $118.4 million, up 23% year-over-year, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of growth. The company raised its outlook for AI-enabled discovery orders, now expecting to meet or exceed triple-digit percentage growth for fiscal 2026, and also pointed to potential triple-digit growth in fiscal 2027. NGS Applications segment saw accelerating momentum, with academic/government segment growing 32% versus last quarter's 3%.

Tyson Foods reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.99, up 9% year-over-year, and total sales of $13.9 billion, essentially flat. Segment operating income of $779 million rose $18 million, driven by chicken, pork, and international, but beef posted a $138 million loss. Prepared Foods volume grew for the third consecutive quarter, while chicken segment operating income grew $40 million to $488 million. Guidance was not explicitly provided in the excerpt, though management noted improved cost benefits expected in Q4 and into fiscal 2027 for Prepared Foods.

Sally Beauty reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $935 million, approximately flat YoY, with flat consolidated comparable sales. Adjusted EPS of $0.55 was up 8% YoY and at the high end of guidance, driven by gross margin expansion. Sally segment grew comps 1.6% (U.S./Canada +3.5%), while BSG comps declined 2.1%. Full-year guidance was narrowed, with adjusted EPS now expected at $2.04-$2.08, compared to prior range of $2.00-$2.10. Management cited ongoing softness in the hair care category, offset by strength in color and e-commerce growth of 11%.

GeneDx reported Q2 2026 revenue of $114.4M, up 11% Y/Y, with exome and genome revenue up 17% to $100.3M and volume up 32% to 30,785 tests. The company returned to profitability with adjusted net income of $0.4M, one quarter earlier than expected, and reaffirmed full-year guidance. However, the blended ARR was flat at $3,258 and outpatient genome collection rates remained low at approximately 32%, with expectations for meaningful improvement only in Q4.

V2X reported Q2 2026 revenue of $1.26 billion, up 17% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $1.64, up 23% YoY. The company raised full-year guidance for revenue and adjusted EBITDA (approximately 10% growth) and adjusted diluted EPS (16% growth). Strong bookings of $600 million (book-to-bill 0.5x, TTM 1.4x), with $1 billion in awards post-quarter, and a positive Moody's outlook.

Vertex reported 12% year-over-year revenue growth in Q2 2026, driven by CF and new products CASGEVY and JOURNAVX. ALYFTREK surpassed $1 billion in first-half revenue, and CASGEVY grew ~75% sequentially. The company announced the acquisition of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals to add a fifth pillar in rare endocrine diseases. R&D progress includes FDA acceptance of POVI BLA with a November PDUFA date and clearance of IND for VX-017 Type O islet cell therapy.

Douglas Dynamics reported record Q2 2026 results with consolidated net sales up 10% to $214.6 million and adjusted EPS up 7% to $1.22. The Work Truck Attachments segment drove growth with net sales up 20% on strong preseason orders and parts/accessories demand; Work Truck Solutions was relatively flat but remains strong with municipal demand booking into 2027. Management raised full-year guidance and expects a very strong Q3 with a 50/50 preseason shipment split. New capacity investments are on track, while some commercial fleet customers have paused ordering amid geopolitical/economic uncertainty.

MakeMyTrip reported Q1 FY2027 results amid geopolitical and macroeconomic headwinds. Hotels and packages adjusted margin grew 21.3% YoY in constant currency, with standalone hotel volumes up 20.2% and bus ticketing margin up 32.4% YoY. Air ticketing was soft, with international departures down 13% YoY. The company highlighted resilience in domestic travel and reiterated caution for the near term while remaining confident on long-term structural growth.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $644.9 million, up from $533.7 million sequentially, with EPS of $0.70 versus $0.31 in the prior quarter. Gross margin improved to 16.7% from 16.5%, and operating margin rose to 7.0% from 5.1%. Guidance for Q3 is revenue of $700-$750 million and EPS of $0.83-$1.30, implying strong growth. Management raised capacity targets, planning to support a $4 billion revenue run rate by mid-2027 and evaluating expansion for $5 billion.

TKO reported a strong Q2 2026, with record-breaking events like UFC Freedom 250 and FIFA World Cup hospitality sales surpassing $2 billion. Despite a $30 million loss from UFC Freedom 250, management raised full-year guidance, citing robust demand and strategic investments. WWE live events revenue declined due to WrestleMania 42 versus 41, but management framed it as a deliberate investment. The company also announced an additional buyback in the near term.

Q2 2026 revenue: U.S. BRIUMVI net product revenue $228M, up 64% YoY and ~17% QoQ; total revenue $240M, exceeding guidance. Raised full-year U.S. net revenue guidance to $890-$905M, global to ~$950M, and expect Q4 U.S. quarterly revenue exceeding $250M. Positive ENHANCE phase III results support single 600mg infusion initiation; subcu BRIUMVI phase III data expected around year-end/early next year. New MG phase II and schizophrenia phase II studies initiated; azer-cel advancing with >20 patients enrolled.

Supernus and Indivior announced a merger of equals, expected to close in Q4 2026, with Supernus shareholders receiving 1.5401 Indivior shares per Supernus share and Indivior declaring a $1 billion dividend pre-closing. Pro forma combined net revenue is approximately $2.2 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of $888 million (41% margin) including $125 million of expected cost synergies. SUBLOCADE is the largest product at 44% of combined revenue. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, particularly for SUBLOCADE, citing improved commercial execution and increased patient awareness.

Stoke Therapeutics reported significant progress in its phase III EMPEROR study for zorevunersen in Dravet syndrome, with enrollment completed at 162 patients in just 10 months and no treatment discontinuations. The company is on track for a phase III readout in Q3 2027 and plans a rolling NDA submission starting Q1 2027. Long-term OLE data show durable seizure control and statistically significant improvements in cognition and behavior through four years, with a strong safety profile. The company has a pro forma cash position of approximately $420 million, providing runway to a potential U.S. launch by early 2028. Additionally, STK-002 for ADOA has completed dosing of the first cohort and is advancing to higher doses, with early results expected in the first half of 2027.

Palantir delivered record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 93% YoY to $1.935 billion, the highest growth rate ever, and adjusted free cash flow of $1.22 billion. U.S. commercial revenue accelerated 149% YoY with record TCV bookings of $2.132 billion. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.154 billion (82% growth) and U.S. commercial guidance to at least $3.424 billion (134% growth), marking the largest guidance raise in company history.

Sportradar reported Q2 2026 revenue of EUR 378 million, up 19% YoY (21% constant currency), with adjusted EBITDA up 19% to EUR 76 million, margin at 20%. Growth was driven by betting content (up 27%) and IMG ARENA synergies, but U.S. growth moderated and rest-of-world faced tax headwinds. Despite strong momentum in prediction markets and recent Kalshi/Polymarket deals, management lowered full-year guidance due to these headwinds, while raising expectations for prediction market revenue in 2027.

Snap reported Q2 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 19% year-over-year, with advertising revenue up 9% to $1.28 billion and other revenue up 85% to $316 million. Gross margin expanded to 58%, adjusted EBITDA was $250 million, and free cash flow was $121 million. Management raised full-year infrastructure cost guidance and guided Q3 revenue of $1.70-$1.74 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $300-$350 million, while expressing confidence in durable growth and a new focus on free cash flow per share.

Clorox reported Q4 FY2026 with organic sales flat or up slightly as categories remained soft; consumption returned to flat in Q4. Inflation is expected to exceed $200 million in FY2027, more than double historical range, with Brent at $90/barrel. GOJO (Purell) is performing ahead of plan and accretive in Q4, but outlook reflects muted category growth and a Q1 timing blip in Kingsford. Management expects momentum to build through FY2027 with continued market share progress and productivity offsetting inflation in SG&A.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was a record $360.7 million, up 28.8% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $48.8 million, up 54% YoY and a 41.3% margin. Contribution profit rose 26.3% to $118.1 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, contribution profit, and adjusted EBITDA, and cited strong bookings and backlog extending into 2027.

Marriott reported strong Q2 2026 results with global RevPAR up 3.4%, above expectations, led by a 5% increase in U.S. and Canada, the highest in 13 quarters. Adjusted diluted EPS rose 20% to $3.19, and adjusted EBITDA increased 13% to $1.59 billion. The company raised full-year 2026 global RevPAR guidance to 3%-3.5% and gross fee guidance to $6.03-$6.06 billion, reflecting broad-based demand and World Cup tailwinds. New U.S. co-branded credit card agreements with JPMorgan Chase and American Express are expected to add about $30 million in 2026 fees, though Middle East conflict continues to weigh on EMEA.

Kosmos Energy reported strong Q2 2026 results with production up 12% year-on-year and absolute operating costs down around 25%, driven by new Jubilee wells and GTA ramp-up. Jubilee's J76 well is the best in over a decade, and production is trending to the upper end of guidance. Net debt reduced ~50% from year-end 2025, and the company completed a Tiberius farm-down, de-risking capex. Full-year production guidance was adjusted for the Equatorial Guinea sale, but core assets remain on track.

Q2 2026 net income was $174 million, up from $158 million in Q1, with adjusted EBITDA of $314 million versus $300 million. Revenues grew modestly, and gross margin held at 85%, well above the 75% target, partly helped by lower OpEx and maintenance phasing. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed: adjusted EBITDA of $1.225-$1.275 billion (flat), adjusted FCF of $910-$960 million (20% YoY growth at midpoint), and $280 million of excess FCF. Volumes are expected to grow at least 5% in the second half, but Q3 EBITDA is guided roughly flat as higher revenues are offset by higher OpEx, with Q4 expected to improve.

Ibotta's Q2 FY2026 revenue came in at $88.9 million, up 3% year-over-year and above guidance, with redemption revenue up 10% YoY. Total redeemers grew 21% YoY to 20.9 million, and third-party redemption revenue jumped 27% YoY. The company returned to year-over-year revenue growth a quarter earlier than expected, citing improved offer supply and stronger go-to-market execution, including the LiveLift product and seasonal events playbook.

Supernus and Indivior announced a merger of equals, with expected annual cost synergies of $125 million. Combined pro forma net revenue is approximately $2.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA $888 million (41% margin) for trailing twelve months. Indivior shareholders will own ~56.5% of the combined company, and the transaction is expected to close in Q4 2026. Management emphasizes complementary portfolios, strong balance sheet, and scale for future business development.

Inspire Medical Systems reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $200.6 million, down 7.6% year-over-year, due to coding and reimbursement disruption. Despite the decline, adjusted operating income exceeded expectations, supported by disciplined cost management and gross margin expansion from a higher mix of Inspire V. The company raised its 2026 revenue, adjusted operating margin, and adjusted EPS guidance. Management is executing Project Horizon, a growth investment plan expected to create $30 million in annualized investment capacity, and is encouraged by improving prior authorization trends and proposed 2027 CMS reimbursement increases, though final rates are pending.

Jazz Pharmaceuticals delivered record revenue of $1.2 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with double-digit growth across key brands: XYWAV +13% to $471M, Epidiolex +16% to $292M, Zepzelca +42% to $106M, and Ziihera generating $15M. Management raised full-year revenue guidance and expects XYWAV to grow double-digit for the year, revised from flat to up mid-single digits. The company anticipates FDA submission for zanidatamab in GEA with a PDUFA date of August 25, 2026, and is preparing for a potential launch.

In Q2 FY2026, Ichor reported revenue of $294.8 million, up 15% sequentially, with gross margin of 14.1% exceeding guidance and EPS of $0.34, the highest in three years. The company issued its full $200 million ATM equity offering, boosting cash to $256 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth to at least 30%, expects Q3 revenue of $315-$345 million (12% sequential growth at midpoint) and gross margin of 14.5%-15.5%, citing strengthening demand and structural margin improvements.

Ethos Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $189.6 million, up 113% year-over-year, with direct channel revenue up 131% and third-party channel up 90%. Adjusted EBITDA was $35.2 million (19% margin), and the company raised full-year revenue guidance to $727-$731 million (88% growth at midpoint) and EBITDA to $119-$123 million. The board authorized a $100 million share repurchase program.

Krystal Biotech reported Q2 2026 U.S. net revenue of $91.6 million for VYJUVEK and over 730 U.S. reimbursement approvals, surpassing a 60% penetration target. International revenue was broadly flat due to a reserve provision from German pricing negotiations, but management highlighted strong underlying demand. Clinical pipeline progresses with two registrational studies nearing readouts (KB803 in DEB, KB801 in NK) and plans to start registrational studies for CF and HHD in 2027. The company remains in a strong financial position and continues to invest in global expansion and pipeline development.

Lindblad reported Q2 2026 revenue of $199.2 million, up 18.6% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up 30.7% to $32.5 million, and margins expanding 150 basis points to 16.3%. Occupancy hit 91% and net yield reached a record $1,294 per guest night. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $830-$860 million and net yield guidance to 4.5%-5.5%, while reaffirming EBITDA guidance. Management highlighted double-digit growth across both segments, a strong 2028 launch with bookings double the prior year, and continued cost innovation despite fuel price headwinds.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Operating EPS grew 45% to $1.26, leading to an 8% increase in full-year 2026 EPS guidance.
2. Achieved 16th consecutive quarter of sales growth, with Medicare Supplement NAP up 52% and Worksite division NAP up 29%.
3. Net investment income grew 8%, with the new money rate at 6.16%, marking the 14th consecutive quarter above 6%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Life NAP in the Consumer division declined 9% year-over-year, driven by lower direct-to-consumer sales as the company shifts away from TV advertising.
2. Acknowledged difficult upcoming sales comparisons for the Consumer division, creating uncertainty around continuing the multi-quarter growth streak.
3. Supplemental health margins were partially offset by a handful of large claims, though management characterized them as isolated events.
rows.key_quote: Earnings benefited from strong insurance product margin and investment results reflecting growth in the business and expansion of the portfolio book yield.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Q2 sales up 53% (47% organic) driven by the infrastructure vertical which more than doubled, led by massive data center demand. 2. Full-year guidance was significantly raised for sales (to 37-39% growth from 26-28%) and adjusted EPS (to $5.00-$5.10 from $4.45-$4.55). 3. Announced a third liquid cooling capacity expansion (Blaine 2) to meet demand, projecting data center sales to reach $2 billion in 2026.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Electrical Connections segment return on sales declined 140 bps year-over-year due to inflation and mix. 2. Full-year tariff impact forecast increased to approximately $100 million from $80 million due to higher volumes. 3. Data center orders are characterized as 'large and lumpy,' causing potential quarter-to-quarter variability in growth rates.
rows.key_quote: The better than expected sales were primarily driven by the infrastructure vertical, led by data centers, along with stronger demand in our short cycle business.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Closed the transformational acquisition of Flushing Financial, adding $8.7B in assets and significantly expanding its NYC footprint. 2. Core EPS of $0.43 was up 39% year-over-year, and Net Interest Margin expanded 12 basis points to 3.05%. 3. Provided strong forward guidance for NIM expansion to 3.09%-3.14% in Q4 and expense reductions as merger synergies are realized.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported a GAAP net loss of $0.04 per share, driven by $33.6 million in after-tax merger-related expenses. 2. Excluding the acquisition, total deposits declined modestly due to seasonal government outflows and a reduction in brokered deposits. 3. Management acknowledged that competitive pressures are keeping spreads on new loans at "historically tight levels".
rows.key_quote: This performance was driven by the addition of Flushing, which contributed $19 million of net interest income.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.positive_highlights:
1. Hedging & Optimization: The gas fleet realized an average price of $68/MWh, a 134% premium to the $29/MWh average spot price, demonstrating successful margin protection. 
2. Strategic M&A: Announced the acquisition of two Colorado gas peakers with long-term contracts, expected to add $110 million in low-risk annual adjusted EBITDA. 
3. Data Center Strategy Progress: Favorable government regulations now allow the grid operator (AESO) to advance plans for using TransAlta's underutilized assets to serve AI-driven power demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Alberta Power Market: Spot prices averaged just $29/MWh, down from $40/MWh in the prior year, pressuring merchant revenues. 
2. Hydro Segment Decline: The Hydro segment's adjusted EBITDA fell by $39 million year-over-year, primarily due to lower Alberta spot and hedge prices. 
3. Credit Rating Outlook Downgrade: S&P shifted its rating outlook to negative, citing the soft Alberta market and the temporary offline status of the Centralia facility.
rows.key_quote: Our gas fleet realized an average price of $68 per megawatt hour, a significant 134% premium to the average spot price.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record AUM reached $162.9B, up 7% sequentially, driven by $3.1B in net inflows and the Atlantic House acquisition.
2. Adjusted operating margin expanded 900 bps YoY to 41.1% (YTD), demonstrating significant operating leverage and scalability.
3. Revenue grew 57% and adjusted EPS grew 72% year-over-year, reflecting strong organic growth and successful strategic initiatives.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lowered full-year interest income guidance to $8M from $10M due to reallocation of cash to share repurchases.
2. European trading activity, a component of other revenues, has become more moderate compared to prior periods.
3. Ceres flows were low at $5M in a 'transition quarter' as its flagship fund closed to new investment and Fund II launched.
rows.key_quote: Growth came from both the U.S. and Europe...no single product or market drove the quarter. That diversification matters because it makes the business more durable.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year outlook for Operating EBITDA (to $4.1B-$4.3B) and Operating EPS (to $3.60-$3.80), an 11% increase at the midpoint. 2. Strong H1 results with sales +4%, operating EBITDA +10%, and EPS +14%, with operating EBITDA margin expanding nearly 200 basis points. 3. Cost performance and productivity were the largest driver of H1 EBITDA growth, contributing over $160 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Crop Protection pricing remains under pressure, declining low-single digits in H1 and expected to decline low-to-mid single digits in H2, primarily due to competition in Brazil. 2. Brazil corn area is expected to be flat, a slowdown from the low-single-digit expansion seen in prior years. 3. Tight credit and input cost pressures are impacting farmer margins in Brazil, causing delays in purchasing decisions.
rows.key_quote: Cost performance remained the largest contributor adding more than $160 million through lower input cost, manufacturing efficiencies, and continued productivity initiatives.

Sony reported record Q1 FY2026 results with consolidated sales up 8% YoY to JPY 2,837.8 billion and operating income up 40% to JPY 476.5 billion. The company raised its full-year sales forecast 2% to JPY 12,500 billion, operating income forecast 8% to JPY 1,720 billion, and net income forecast 4% to JPY 1,210 billion, partly driven by expected U.S. tariff refunds of about JPY 80 billion. G&NS, Music, and I&SS posted record first-quarter operating profits; however, management is cautious on I&SS due to memory market conditions and the Kumamoto earthquake impact is not yet incorporated into forecasts.

RBC Bearings reported a strong fiscal Q1 2027 with net sales up 19.2% to $519.5M, adjusted EPS up 36.6% to $3.88, and adjusted EBITDA up 28.1% to $181.2M. Aerospace & Defense revenue grew 36.9% (16.6% organic) while Industrial grew 8.4%. Management guided Q2 revenue of $505-515M (10.9-13.1% growth) and adjusted gross margins of 45.5-45.75%. They highlighted strong demand in space and marine, with backlog of $2.3B and plans to pay off remaining term loan by November 2026.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Engineered Solutions segment achieved record performance with sales up 9% and a record operating margin of 17.8%, driven by a 14% increase in Refractories sales.
2. Environmental and Infrastructure sales grew 19% year-to-date, showing strong recovery with building materials sales up 41% and drilling products up 20% in the quarter.
3. Key growth projects are advancing, with the bleaching earth expansion for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) now fully ramped and three new paper satellite facilities contributing to revenue.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant margin compression from a price/cost lag, where cost increases of $16 million (freight, energy) outpaced pricing benefits of $8 million, primarily impacting the Consumer & Specialty segment.
2. The company recorded a $290 million charge to increase its reserve for the talc litigation related to its BMI OldCo subsidiary.
3. Consumer & Specialty segment sales were weaker than expected, declining slightly due to moderated cat litter orders and a shift in a personal care customer campaign.
rows.key_quote: Pricing contributed $8 million to income. However, overall cost increases totaled $16 million in the quarter as we experienced higher freight and energy costs.

Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue was $610M, up 9.5% year-over-year and a record, with record shipments of 5,657 units and backlog up over 50% sequentially and year-over-year. Demand momentum continued from March, with double-digit sequential order growth across all regions and channels. Factory-built gross margin declined 40 basis points sequentially due to higher manufacturing costs and retail pricing competition in Texas. EPS was $5.43, down from $6.42 a year ago, with higher tax rate and lower interest income. Company repurchased $30M in stock, and AM Best raised its outlook. Management is optimistic about the new 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act and state-level zoning reforms.

Standex reported Q4 FY2026 sales of $228.3 million, up 7.7% organically, with record adjusted EPS of $2.45 and record free cash flow of $35 million. Full-year organic sales grew 5.5%, adjusted operating margin reached 19.4%, and adjusted EPS was $8.74, all records. Management guided to mid-to-high single-digit sales growth for FY2027 with continued margin expansion, and detailed grid capacity expansion targeting $340-$440 million in sales by fiscal 2030. A&D margins improved 410 bps in Q4 to 22.5%, but Q1 A&D revenue is expected to be moderately lower on project timing.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Workforce Solutions (WFS) has over $2 billion in formal bids outstanding in Canada, representing more than double the company's available fleet capacity.
2. Consolidated revenue grew 23% to $129.2 million, driven by strong lodging revenue from the Royal Camp acquisition and a 17% increase in consolidated rental revenue.
3. LodgeLink delivered a record quarter, with total trade value increasing 69% to $43.5 million, reflecting strong customer adoption and platform momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted EPS declined 50% to $0.09 from $0.18, and GAAP EPS was $0.01 vs $0.15 a year ago.
2. Consolidated margins moderated due to a revenue mix shift toward lower-margin lodging services from the Royal Camp acquisition, causing EBITDA growth (4%) to significantly lag revenue growth (23%).
3. WFS sales revenue declined 70% and MSS sales declined 18% due to a strategic decision to preserve fleet for future rental opportunities and softness in the U.S. education sector.
rows.key_quote: WFS currently has more than $2 billion of formal bids outstanding...representing more than 2x the company's current available fleet capacity.

Moog reported record Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.1B, up 15% YoY, and record adjusted EPS of $3.72, up 60%, boosted by a $30M tariff refund and tax benefits. Each segment grew, with industrial up 18% driven by data center cooling, and the company raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted operating margin, EPS, and free cash flow. Demand is strong across defense, commercial aerospace, and industrial, with a generational inflection in defense spending and a data center cooling revenue ramp expected to nearly quadruple within a year.

ExxonMobil reported exceptional Q2 results despite losing ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict, with industry-leading earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B. Upstream production outside the Middle East hit a two-decade high, chemicals margins surged ~180% QoQ, and specialty products posted record earnings. Guyana's Errea Wittu FPSO on track, and the company achieved $16.3B cumulative structural cost savings since 2019. Guidance implies continued momentum with free cash flow expected to double by 2030 versus 2025.

Weyerhaeuser reported Q2 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.23 and adjusted EPS of $0.13, with adjusted EBITDA of $310 million. Timberlands EBITDA rose slightly sequentially, while Wood Products improved $58 million quarter-over-quarter, driven by stronger lumber pricing, but OSB posted a $6 million loss due to higher costs. Strategic Land Solutions EBITDA fell $64 million sequentially on lower Climate Solutions contributions, but full-year SLS guidance was raised to approximately $450 million. Management noted transportation constraints, elevated fuel costs, and cautious OSB buyer sentiment, with third-quarter Timberlands EBITDA expected slightly higher.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Announced and pending backlog grew nearly 2.5x year-over-year, signaling a strong future revenue pipeline. 
2. Total booked plus announced and pending backlog increased by over 30% year-over-year, reinforcing the positive outlook for H2 2026 and 2027. 
3. Management observed significantly improved M&A sentiment, stating boardrooms have removed 'historic barriers' and are now in 'transaction mode'.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. First-half revenues of $305 million were down 17% compared to the prior year, reflecting weak current-period performance. 
2. The adjusted compensation ratio for the first half was high at 71%, well above the full-year target of 67%, indicating pressure on profitability. 
3. Some large fee events in the backlog are not expected to close in 2026, pushing revenue recognition into 2027.
rows.key_quote: Our announced and pending backlog... This metric is up nearly 2.5x from a year ago.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. O&P Americas EBITDA quadrupled YoY, driven by a record $0.30/lb polyethylene price increase in April due to global supply disruptions from the Middle East conflict.
2. Achieved an impressive consolidated 23% EBITDA margin, demonstrating the leverage of a reshaped portfolio and cost cuts in favorable market conditions.
3. Strong operational execution with O&P Americas crackers running at ~95% utilization, maximizing production to capture significant margin opportunities.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Intermediates & Derivatives segment was severely impacted by an unplanned outage at the Bayport PO/TBA asset, resulting in an estimated $250 million EBITDA loss.
2. The Technology segment outlook is weakening, with Q3 EBITDA expected to moderate due to normalizing catalyst sales and 'almost nonexistent' new licensing opportunities.
3. Ongoing reliability issues at the La Porte syngas unit continue to negatively affect acetic acid and VAM production.
rows.key_quote: This was primarily a result of a $0.30 per pound increase in polyethylene contract prices...driven by global supply disruptions from the conflict.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Significant EPS beat: Adjusted EPS of $3.67 was ~$1.00 above guidance, driven by a $0.63 tariff refund and operational outperformance.
2. Strong revenue growth and share gains: Net sales grew 6.8% YoY, with volume benefiting from initial stocking of new, successful product placements across all segments.
3. Margin Expansion: Adjusted gross margin increased 100 bps YoY to 27.4% and adjusted operating margin rose 170 bps, as pricing and productivity offset underlying inflation.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Cautious Q3 Outlook: Guided Q3 adjusted EPS to $2.50-$2.60, a significant sequential decline, anticipating a 'more pronounced' seasonal sales drop from a strong Q2.
2. Rising Input Costs: Management expects a significant step-up in input cost headwinds in Q3, similar to the jump from Q1 to Q2, pressuring margins.
3. Persistently Soft End Markets: The residential market remains weak, with home resales near multi-decade lows and new construction soft, with no near-term recovery anticipated.
rows.key_quote: Volume benefited from initial stocking of new product placements and limited increases in inventory by some customers ahead of announced price increases.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive Growth Pipeline: Sanctioned $9 billion in new projects in 2026, part of a $41 billion secured backlog and a broader $50 billion opportunity set through 2030.
2. Strong Gas Transmission Demand: Project Beacon's open season "significantly exceeded...initial expectations" from power, data center, and utility customers, signaling robust demand in the U.S. Northeast.
3. High Asset Utilization & Successful Recontracting: Mainline volumes averaged a strong 3.1 million barrels per day, and the company successfully recontracted the majority of volumes on its Spearhead and Flanagan South pipelines into the 2030s and 2040s.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. MLO2 Project Postponement: The upstream portion of the Mainline Optimization 2 (MLO2) project has been postponed, with the company pivoting to focus on downstream segments first due to producer and policy timing.
2. Pressure on Earnings and Balance Sheet: EPS was slightly down YoY due to higher depreciation and interest expense. Debt-to-EBITDA ended the quarter at 5.1x, above the 4.5x-5.0x target range, though attributed to FX.
3. Identified Headwinds: Management noted headwinds for the full year from lower market access contributions in the Liquids Pipelines (LP) segment and the impact of higher U.S. interest rates.
rows.key_quote: We're hearing from customers...looking for additional capacity to support unprecedented power and LNG demand.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Executed a $1.625B California portfolio sale, reinvesting proceeds into newer Sunbelt assets and $694M of share repurchases, with the strategy being FFO-accretive after year one.
2. Identified significant operational improvements ('green shoots'), with blended lease rate growth turning positive in June/July and system-wide signed new leases achieving positive growth on some days in July for the first time in years.
3. Improved full-year same-store NOI guidance (ex-California) from a 0.9% decline to a 0.6% decline, driven by better expense control.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 new lease rates remained negative at -3.3%, indicating that while improving, pricing pressure still exists.
2. Full-year same-store NOI is still projected to decline by 0.6% (ex-California), showing the market has not yet fully recovered to positive growth.
3. Key markets like Austin and Nashville continue to work through significant new supply, which leads to concessions and tempers rent growth despite improving demand.
rows.key_quote: I'm happy to report that system-wide average signed new leases have been positive a handful days this month... and that is a very green shoot.

In Q2 2026, Vale reported pro forma EBITDA of $4.1 billion, up 19% year-on-year, with Vale Base Metals EBITDA nearly 80% higher at $1.3 billion. Iron ore production reached highest second-quarter levels since 2018, copper production was strongest in nine years, and nickel production rose 4% year-on-year. The company raised shareholder returns with $1.7 billion in dividends and a new buyback program, but raised 2026 iron ore cost guidance due to FX and oil headwinds, while lowering copper and nickel cost guidance. Growth projects like Serra Sul +20 started up and Bacaba is expected earlier than planned.

rows.positive_highlights:
Revenue grew 23% YoY to $37.1M and Adjusted EBITDA grew 48% with margins expanding 400 bps to 21%.
Successfully brought 2 million employees from client Vensure Employer Solutions live on the payroll tax management platform.
Organic growth improved to 5% from 1% YoY, with management guiding to double-digit organic recurring revenue growth in H2 2026.
rows.negative_highlights:
Organic growth slowed sequentially from 7% in Q1 to 5% in Q2, attributed to seasonality.
Tough year-over-year comparisons on non-recurring professional services revenue are expected to mute total revenue growth in H2 2026.
Non-GAAP gross margin was flat year-over-year at 73%, though GAAP gross margin improved by 200 bps.
rows.key_quote: In quarter two, we grew revenue by 23% and adjusted EBITDA an impressive 48% with increased scale in AI and efficiencies.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Production Growth & Reliability: Global Upstream production grew over 5% Q/Q, driven by exceptional reliability and new records in U.S. production (~2.1M BOE/d). 
2. Cost & Synergy Execution: Achieved its $3 billion structural cost reduction target 6 months early and captured $1.5 billion in Hess synergies (50% above target), also 6 months ahead of schedule. 
3. New Power Venture: Signed a 20-year, 2.67 GW power purchase agreement with Microsoft for Project Kilby, establishing a new business line with expected mid-teens returns.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Geopolitical Risk: Ongoing conflicts in the Black Sea (affecting CPC pipeline) and Middle East create operational uncertainty, though current direct impact is described as minimal. 
2. China Demand Uncertainty: Management characterized China's demand situation as a "black box," representing a significant unknown variable for global markets. 
3. Venezuela Dependency: Future growth in Venezuela is contingent on negotiating a new, more competitive fiscal framework, and full debt recovery is not expected until early 2027.
rows.key_quote: Global Upstream production grew more than 5% quarter-over-quarter, underpinned by exceptional reliability across key assets.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Exceptional growth from key immunology assets: SKYRIZI sales grew 24% to $5.5 billion and RINVOQ sales grew 23.7% to over $2.5 billion, both exceeding expectations. 2) Robust Neuroscience performance: The portfolio grew over 20%, with Vraylar, Botox Therapeutic, and the oral CGRP franchise all delivering double-digit sales growth. 3) Raised full-year revenue guidance: The company increased its full-year revenue forecast by $300 million, reflecting strong momentum across its growth platform.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Continued HUMIRA decline: Sales fell 36.1% operationally to $706 million due to ongoing biosimilar competition. 2) IMBRUVICA pressure: Sales declined 29.4% due to IRA pricing impact and competitive share pressure, contributing to a 2.4% drop in the overall oncology portfolio. 3) Juvederm weakness: Global sales for the dermal filler were down 6.6% due to continued headwinds in key markets, weighing on the aesthetics segment.
rows.key_quote: The performance of SKYRIZI, RINVOQ, and our neuroscience portfolio continues to be very strong. With each delivering growth above 20%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised Guidance: Core FFO per share guidance midpoint was increased by $0.03 to $1.95, driven by superior operational performance and capital allocation.
2. Strong Operational Execution: Same-Home controllable expense growth was held under 1%, while blended rent spreads accelerated to 2.7% in Q2 and 2.8% in July.
3. Successful Development & Dispositions: Record pre-leasing of new homes (40% of H2 deliveries already leased) and disposition proceeds tracking to the high end of the $400M-$600M range.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Implied Revenue Deceleration: Guidance implies a slowdown in revenue growth for the second half of the year, attributed to the burn-off of high rent growth earn-in from 2025.
2. Market-Specific Softness: Management noted Atlanta and Tampa are not portfolio 'bright spots,' with Atlanta's rates 'treading water a little bit.'
3. Slower H2 Development Deliveries: The full-year delivery guide was held flat despite strong results, implying a lower delivery cadence in H2 compared to H1.
rows.key_quote: FFO growth was driven by growing leasing spreads and occupancy while holding year-over-year controllable expense growth to less than 1%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Favorable Chlor-Alkali Pricing: Geopolitical conflict led to supply disruptions, resulting in significantly higher export pricing for caustic soda and EDC, which was a "second quarter bright spot." 2. Epoxy Turnaround: The segment returned to profitability, posting its best results in over 3 years, driven by price increases and over $50 million in annual cost savings. 3. Winchester Recovery: The division showed improved year-over-year commercial demand and successful price increases to offset rising metal costs, complemented by strong military sales.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Unplanned VCM Outage: A shutdown at the Freeport, Texas VCM plant resulted in a $40 million penalty to Q2 adjusted EBITDA, with a further $20 million impact expected in Q3. 2. Weak European Demand: European demand for Epoxy remained flat and weak, with no near-term market recovery expected due to high energy costs. 3. Q3 Price Normalization: Management expects export prices for EDC and caustic soda to trend lower in Q3 from their Q2 peaks, creating a headwind.
rows.key_quote: Caustic soda and EDC export pricing was a second quarter bright spot reflecting the supply chain disruptions at the beginning of the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance to $18.2B and $9.30 respectively, driven by broad strength and the Superior acquisition.
2. Achieved record backlog of $21.4 billion, a $5 billion YoY increase, fueled by "unprecedented demand" in mission-critical infrastructure.
3. Strong segmental growth, with Clean Energy & Infrastructure revenue up 43% and Power Delivery revenue up 20% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Communications segment is facing "short-term pressure," resulting in a lowered full-year revenue outlook for the segment.
2. The Communications weakness is driven by a pause in wireless spending ahead of new spectrum rollouts and delays in new wireline projects.
3. Communications segment margins in Q2 were hurt by execution challenges and higher indirect fuel and equipment costs.
rows.key_quote: Everything tied to mission critical is doing extremely well right now.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record leasing volume of 819,000 sq ft in Q2 with strong cash rent spreads of 15% (28% straight-line).
FFO per share grew 7% YoY to $1.88, leading to a raised full-year FFO guidance to a midpoint of $7.52.
Small shop occupancy increased 100 basis points to 92.3%, with a strong leasing pipeline of over 1.5 million sq ft indicating future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
Forecasted G&A expenses were increased by $2 million due to investments in digital innovation and business development teams.
Guidance incorporated a $0.01 to $0.02 per share headwind from a more conservative interest rate outlook.
A onetime investment write-off of $0.015 per share negatively impacted the quarter's results.
rows.key_quote: We are reporting 124 comparable deals for 819k square feet with cash rent 15% higher and 28% higher on a straight-line basis.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Completed the sale of Aquarion, generating $1.7 billion in net proceeds to strengthen the balance sheet and focus on being a pure-play regulated utility. 2. Moody's upgraded the company's outlook to stable from negative, affirming its financial strategy. 3.
