Preliminarily selected for a joint transmission project with a ~$700 million share for Eversource, providing a new long-term growth opportunity.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Recognized a $164 million after-tax charge related to cost increases on the Revolution Wind project due to stop-work orders. 2. Q2 recurring earnings were negatively impacted by a lower base ROE rate in the Electric Transmission segment ordered by FERC. 3. Connecticut regulators denied the recovery of carrying charges associated with storm costs.
rows.key_quote: Lower earnings in the transmission business were primarily driven by the base ROE rate reduction ordered by FERC back in March.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Pharma segment resilience: Excluding the emergency medicine headwind, Pharma core sales grew 8%, driven by injectables (GLP-1s, biologics) and a 15% core sales increase in Consumer Healthcare.
2. Strong underlying demand: Momentum continues in high-value areas like GLP-1 therapies (used by 11% of Americans), prestige fragrance, and beverage dispensing for bottled water.
3. EPS beat and positive guidance: Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.42 beat guidance, and the company guided Q3 EPS to a higher range of $1.45-$1.53, expecting the emergency medicine headwind to ease.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant margin compression: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell 190 bps YoY to 20.7%. Margins declined across all segments: Pharma (-180 bps), Beauty (-190 bps), and Closures (-200 bps).
2. Major emergency medicine headwind: An anticipated decline in high-margin emergency medicine sales drove a 15% YoY decrease in adjusted EPS and was the primary cause of Pharma's margin drop.
3. Persistent operational challenges: Beauty and Closures segments continue to suffer from operational issues, including challenges in Beauty's American operations and ramp-up costs in Closures, with no clear timeline for resolution.
rows.key_quote: Pharma's margin decline was...driven by...unfavourable product mix, primarily due to the decline in high margin emergency medicine sales.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record quarterly revenue of $1.6B (25% growth), driven by strong performance across all construction sectors, especially Utilities.
2. Adjusted EBITDA doubled to $82M as Construction segment adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 5.5% from 3.1% last year.
3. Upgraded full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 'double-digit growth' based on a $10.5B backlog and a pipeline of lower-risk, collaborative projects.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported a GAAP diluted loss per share of $1.58, caused by a one-time, non-cash $128M fair value adjustment on the Aecon Utilities share purchase.
2. Concessions segment adjusted EBITDA declined to $11M from $16M year-over-year due to lower fees from recently completed projects.
3. Legacy projects continued to drag on results, contributing a negative gross profit of $4.5M in the quarter.
rows.key_quote: The increase was driven by improved gross profit margin in urban transportation and civil, plus higher volumes in utilities.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record AUM of $912 billion, driven by equity and private market growth. 
Equity assets reached a record $110 billion, with MDT strategies generating $3.5 billion in net sales. 
The acquisition of FCP added $3.2 billion in private market assets, and a strong institutional pipeline of $3.4 billion is set for Q3.
rows.negative_highlights:
Total money market assets decreased by $7.9 billion (1%) from Q1, driven by seasonal outflows. 
Equity segment saw overall net redemptions of $1.1 billion, although this was caused by an expected $3 billion sub-advisory redemption. 
One-time acquisition costs related to FCP negatively impacted net income by approximately $0.06 per share.
rows.key_quote: Equity sales were again led by our MDT strategies. MDT had a record $6 billion of gross sales and over $3.5 billion in net sales.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year guidance for revenue (to $23.8B), operating income (to $1.14B), and free cash flow (to $640M).
2. Secured a significant seating conquest award with Audi and expanded business with Chinese OEMs like Leapmotor, contributing to $2.9B in YTD awards.
3. E-Systems margins expanded 90 basis points year-over-year, driven by strong net operating performance of 155 basis points.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Deteriorating market conditions in China, with management embedding 'continued weakness' into the H2 outlook after the domestic market fell 20% in H1.
2. Muted growth expectations for 2027 due to the wind-down of non-core E-Systems products ($235M revenue impact) and challenging production volume comparisons.
3. The full-year global production outlook was revised down to -2% (Lear-weighted) from -1%, primarily due to lower assumptions for China.
rows.key_quote: E-Systems margins expanded a significant 90 basis points, driven by a strong 155 basis points of net performance.

VEON reported Q2 revenue of $1.27 billion, up 17% year-on-year, and EBITDA of $552 million, up 6.2%, with digital revenue surging 53.6% to $342 million. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting revenue growth of 15%-18% and EBITDA growth of 9%-12%. Management highlighted strong cash generation, with operating cash flow up 238% in the quarter, and announced a new annual share cancellation commitment of at least $100 million.

Franklin Resources reported Q3 FY2026 with record AUM of $1.8 trillion and $18.4 billion in long-term net inflows, with positive flows across every asset class and geography. Adjusted operating income rose 7% quarter-over-quarter and 35% year-over-year to $508.9 million. Private markets fundraising reached $33 billion year-to-date, exceeding the original full-year target, and management raised guidance to ~$40 billion. The company returned $521.5 million to shareholders, including $348.1 million in share repurchases, and announced a corporate name change to Franklin Templeton, Inc. Management expressed confidence in margin expansion toward 30%+ and noted a potential investor day later this year or early next.

TELUS reported Q2 2026 results amid a leadership transition, highlighting macroeconomic headwinds from lower immigration and an industry-wide demand slowdown. The company announced a 55% dividend cut, a new leverage target of 3x or lower by end of 2028, and a target of at least 10% compounded annual free cash flow growth in 2027 and 2028. Management is focusing on balance sheet strength, cost discipline, and portfolio monetization, with more details on cost structure expected by Q3 2026.

Erie Indemnity reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $180M ($3.45 per diluted share) versus $175M ($3.34) a year ago, with operating income up 2.5%. The Exchange combined ratio improved to 103.9% from 116.9%, helped by catastrophe losses falling to 15 points from 22 points. Direct written premium growth slowed to 3.3% from 9.2%, and policies in force declined 2% with retention at 87.5%. Management highlighted continued rollout of Erie Secure Auto (now in 10 states), a fully deployed online quoting platform with near-double conversions, and a new teenSMART program.

Cousins Properties reported Q2 FFO of $0.75 per share and raised full-year FFO guidance by $0.01 to $2.95 per share, implying 3.9% growth from 2025. Leasing volume was strong at 924,000 sq ft for the second consecutive quarter, with occupancy at 98.8% leased and cash rent roll-up of 9.2%. The company highlighted improving demand, Sun Belt migration, and limited new supply as tailwinds, and expects to reach 90% occupancy by year-end.

Dominion Energy reported Q2 FY2026 operating earnings of $0.79 per share, including $0.03 of RNG 45Z credits, and reaffirmed all financial guidance. The company highlighted strong demand with over 53 GW of data center capacity in contracting, up 5 GW since year-end. CVOW project cost estimate increased by ~2% to $11.65 billion, with final turbine installation pushed out six months. The NextEra Energy combination is progressing with regulatory filings and hearing schedules set.

T. Rowe Price reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.57, up from $2.52 in Q1 and $2.24 in the year-ago quarter, with AUM of $1.9 trillion and net outflows of $6.5 billion, though flows turned positive in May and June. Revenue rose 8.5% year-over-year to $1.9 billion, and the company raised its full-year expense guidance to up 4%-7%. Investment performance was mixed, with over half of funds beating peers over 1/3/10 years but only 44% over five years. Management highlighted growth in active ETFs and SMAs, which reached $30 billion and $20 billion respectively, and launched new products including a crypto ETF and a private markets fund with Goldman Sachs, while noting ongoing pressure in fundamental active equity.

DiamondRock reported Q2 2026 RevPAR growth of 7%, with Adjusted EBITDA of $107.9 million and Adjusted FFO per share of $0.44, benefiting from a $6.9 million property tax settlement. Excluding the tax benefit, margins expanded 303 basis points, and trailing 12-month free cash flow per share rose 27% year-over-year. The company raised its 2026 guidance for RevPAR growth to 2.5%-4%, Adjusted EBITDA to $310-$320 million, and Adjusted FFO per share to $1.18-$1.23, and increased its quarterly dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share. Management expressed optimism about the transaction market and expects to be active in acquisitions and dispositions over the next 6-12 months.

Q2 2026 gold production of 105k oz and sales of 103k oz, with revenue up to $487M from $452M on a realized gold price of $4,379/oz. Net earnings were $173M ($0.68/sh) and adjusted net earnings $137M ($0.54/sh). Skouries remains on track for first concentrate in Q3, with first ore crushed; McIlvenna Bay achieved first copper and zinc concentrate. Free cash flow was negative $334M due to growth project investment, but underlying operations generated ~$41M. 2026 guidance reaffirmed with higher second-half production expected.

Eastman reported solid volume growth in Advanced Materials and robust volume increases in Chemical Intermediates, with management highlighting strong execution across businesses. The company beat Q2 expectations and expects solid Q3, with full-year earnings outlook better than earlier guidance. However, they reduced the revenue outlook for the circular platform due to capacity constraints and slower-than-expected demand ramp-up. Management noted continued weakness in discretionary end markets but expressed confidence in back-half earnings growth driven by utilization tailwinds and new capacity.

Enbridge reported a solid Q2 2026 with adjusted EBITDA up over CAD 130 million year-over-year, driven by strong volumes and rate case outcomes across all segments. The company reaffirmed 2026 guidance, citing high utilization, favorable recontracting, and a strong project backlog. Management highlighted a CAD 50 billion opportunity set and sanctioned CAD 9 billion of capital in 2026, including Line 5 relocation and Bay Runner Twin. They also noted continued growth in gas transmission and renewables, with an overall positive outlook on North American energy infrastructure demand.

Eaton reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $3.15, a $0.10 beat versus guidance, on record revenue of $8.5 billion with 21% total and 14% organic growth, and segment margins of 23.1%, all above the high end of guidance. The company raised its full-year organic growth guidance by 200 basis points to a midpoint of 12% and adjusted EPS guidance to $13.50 at the midpoint, up $0.22. Demand remains robust with record orders, a total book-to-bill of 1.2, and data center backlog growing to 307 GW. Management expressed strong confidence in continued execution and margin improvement in the second half.

Colgate-Palmolive reported strong Q2 2026 results with top and bottom-line growth, organic sales growth in four of five divisions, and solid gross margin expansion. Free cash flow was up 18% and $1.4 billion was returned to shareholders. Management remains optimistic about second-half momentum despite cost inflation and U.S. softness, and plans to increase brand support in the U.S.

First Business Financial Services reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.84, including a net $0.14 benefit from one-time items; excluding that, EPS grew 26% YoY. Pre-tax pre-provision earnings hit a record $19.8 million, and revenue grew 11% in the first half, exceeding the 10% annual goal. The bank exited its national SBA 7(a) lending, which is expected to add $0.03 per share annually, and maintained full-year guidance for ~10% loan and deposit growth, NIM of 360-365, and fee income growth of 10%.

FET reported Q2 2026 revenue of $226 million, up 8% sequentially, with EBITDA up 39% to $32 million and net income up 148% to $14 million, all exceeding high end of guidance. Orders totaled $236 million with book-to-bill of 104%. The company raised full-year guidance: revenue now expected between $870-$910 million and EBITDA between $115-$125 million, representing 13% and 40% growth respectively versus prior year. Net leverage improved to 1.1x, and management remains confident in 2030 vision, citing market share gains and international expansion.

Q2 2026 EPS was CAD 0.78, up CAD 0.02 YoY, with net earnings of CAD 396 million. The company reaffirmed 7% average annual rate base growth through 2030 and on track for CAD 5.6 billion capital investments in 2026. FortisBC received approval for a larger Tilbury LNG expansion (Phase 1B) with ~CAD 2 billion in regulated rate base, expected in service as early as 2031. TEP continues progress on data center opportunities, with potential incremental generation investment of $1.5-2 billion USD if agreements finalize.

GLPI reported strong Q2 2026 results with AFFO expanding 10% year-over-year and total income from real estate up over $35 million versus Q2 2025. The company increased its dividend by 5% to $0.82 per share and raised 2026 guidance to $4.10-$4.12 per diluted share. Management expressed strong optimism about regional gaming fundamentals and the development pipeline, with leverage at 4.8x and no need to tap equity markets. Development funding guidance of $400-$450 million for the next two quarters remains on track.

Gates reported record Q2 FY2026 sales of $942 million, up 6.6% total and 4.9% core, with adjusted EPS up 13% to $0.44, a quarterly record. Adjusted EBITDA was $211 million at 22.5% margin, modestly above expectations. The company raised full-year core sales growth guidance to 2.5%-4.5% (up 100 bps at midpoint), adjusted EBITDA to $800-$830 million (up $10 million at midpoint), and adjusted EPS to $1.62-$1.70 (up $0.06 at midpoint). Management sees early industrial recovery and expects 6% core growth in H2, with adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 23.5% in H2.

Healthcare Realty reported strong Q2 2026 results, with normalized FFO per share of $0.41, same-store cash NOI growth of 5.1%, and same-store occupancy near 93%. The company raised full-year guidance by $0.02 to $1.64 midpoint and increased same-store NOI outlook to 4.25%-5%. Leasing activity was robust at 1.5 million square feet in the quarter, with cash leasing spreads of 4.8% and retention at 88.5%. The company has raised guidance every quarter since the strategic plan, has reduced leverage and expanded JV acquisitions, and has positive outlook on occupancy and leasing momentum.

Huntsman reported improved margins from Q1 with EBITDA nearly doubled year-over-year, but CEO Peter Huntsman expressed concern over weak demand trends, softening North American housing, languishing Chinese consumer confidence, and rising European energy costs. The company announced a merger of equals with Olin Corporation, targeting $300 million in synergies, and expects Europe PU to be EBITDA positive in Q3, though Middle East volatility and energy inflation pose headwinds. Management continues to push for margins and highlighted growth in Advanced Materials (8%) and Polyurethanes (4%) above underlying markets.

Q2 FY2026 same-store revenue growth accelerated to 0.8%, with move-in rates up 1.7% year-over-year and occupancy gap flat by quarter-end. Same-store NOI growth was negative 0.7% due to 4.4% expense growth, but FFO per share adjusted of $0.63 met guidance. The company raised full-year same-store revenue guidance to 0.5%-1.25% and expects a return to positive earnings growth in the second half, supported by a new Heitman JV contributing 15 non-core assets and ongoing share repurchases.

Church & Dwight reported Q2 FY2026 with organic sales growth of 5.8%, well above the 3% outlook, and adjusted EPS of $0.89, above the $0.88 outlook. Gross margin expanded 40 bps to 45.4%, driven by productivity and acquisitions, partially offset by inflation and tariffs. The company raised its full-year organic sales growth outlook to 4%-5% (from 3%-4%), EPS growth to 6%-8% (from 5%-8%), and cash from operations to $1.175 billion (from $1.15 billion). Management expressed strong confidence in future growth, citing innovation, share gains, and the recent Miss Mouth acquisition.

Ingersoll Rand reported Q2 FY2026 with organic orders up 2%, organic revenue up 4%, and adjusted EPS up 7% to $0.86. Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased 160 bps to 25.4% due to inflation in China, growth investments, and incentive true-up. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to 4.5%-6.5% growth (from prior) and expects EPS near the high end of $3.45-$3.57. Management noted double-digit order growth in early July and announced two acquisitions ($80M combined annual revenue) to strengthen aftermarket capabilities.

BBUC reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $587 million, down slightly from $591 million a year ago, with same-store EBITDA up about 5% and adjusted FFO of $289 million versus $234 million. Management highlighted $1.2 billion in asset sale proceeds, new acquisitions (WFC and Gregg Distributors) at about 10x EBITDA, and a $150 million buyback allocation. CDK debt concerns were addressed by calling the business 'strong' with stable performance, while the company affirmed a $2 billion capital recycling target.

ACCO Brands reported Q2 2026 sales and adjusted EPS above outlook, with consolidated sales up 5% and adjusted operating margin up 20 basis points to 33.1% gross margin. Americas comparable sales grew 2% with strong back-to-school and Mexico performance, while international comps fell 9% due to soft EMEA/Australia and a distribution upgrade disruption. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for reported sales (up 2%-5%) and adjusted EPS ($0.87-$0.91) but maintained a prudent stance on the second half, citing geopolitical uncertainty and higher inflation. EPOS acquisition remains on track with $80M full-year sales and $15M synergies expected, and technology peripherals face short-term demand weakness.

Arbor Realty Trust reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $0.15 per share, in line with guidance, but noted $0.02 per share of one-time financing drag and higher specific reserves. Non-performing assets remained around $1.07 billion, with $90 million resolved in July and $105 million contracted for August. The company closed a $375 million convertible offering, used $114 million to watch back stock at 50% of book value, and cut annual expenses by ~$10 million. Agency origination volume was $1.1 billion in Q2, up 30% year-to-date, but management expects a slower resolution timeline for legacy assets due to elevated rates.

Agree Realty reported record Q2 2026 investment volume of over $500 million across its three platforms, with acquisitions of $451 million at a 7% cap rate and 73% investment-grade tenants. Core FFO per share rose 7.5% to $1.13 and AFFO per share rose 7.4% to $1.14. Full-year AFFO guidance was raised to $4.57-$4.59 and investment volume guidance to $1.6-$1.8 billion. Occupancy set a record at 99.8%, and the company executed 1.6 million square feet of leases in the first half at a 105% recapture rate.

Ameren reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.13, up from $1.01 in the prior year, driven by infrastructure investments, partially offset by higher O&M for tree trimming and maintenance. Management reaffirmed full-year EPS guidance of $5.25-$5.45, noting results are on track. The company highlighted major data center projects from Google and Amazon totaling $25 billion in investment and reiterated its 6%-8% EPS growth outlook. A Missouri rate case requesting $343 million was filed, and a strategic update is planned for the third quarter call.

AutoNation reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $5.56, up from $5.46 a year ago, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth. Revenue was $6.93 billion, essentially flat year-over-year, with after-sales gross profit a record $607 million and CFS per-vehicle profit up 3% to $2,799. The company generated $439 million in adjusted free cash flow for the first half, up 11%, and expects SG&A to reach its 66-67% target by year-end. Management expects adjusted EPS growth in the second half as volume headwinds from tariffs and BEV credits lapse.

Ares delivered a record fundraising quarter with $36B raised, driving AUM and fee-paying AUM up 17% YoY to $671B and $410B respectively. FRE grew 20% and realized income grew over 30%, both at or above long-term growth targets. The company raised its dividend by over 20%, and management remains on track for another record fundraising year with a record pipeline and strong deployment outlook for H2.

AngloGold Ashanti reported Q2 FY2026 with strong financial performance: EBITDA up 46% to $2 billion, headline earnings up 58% to $1 billion, and free cash flow up 36% to $727 million. Total cash costs rose 21% to $1,480/oz, driven by exogenous factors like inflation, higher royalties, and FX, costing about $216/oz. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance, expecting second-half production up about 6% and lower cash costs, with a record dividend of $949 million declared for the half. They also initiated a $2 billion share buyback program and remain focused on cost discipline and organic growth.

Balchem delivered record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of $284M, up 11.2% YoY, and adjusted EPS of $1.49, up 17.3%, both beating expectations. All three segments grew, with Animal Nutrition up 15% and Human Nutrition up 10%. Management raised the credit facility size and repurchased $29M in shares, while expressing confidence in continued growth.

Cameco's Q2 2026 results were lower year-over-year due to the absence of a significant Westinghouse payment related to the Dukovany project in 2025, but the company says underlying fundamentals remain strong. Realized prices improved in both uranium and fuel services segments, the annual production outlook of 19.5-21.5 million pounds is unchanged, and the long-term uranium price reached decade highs. Management highlights strong contracting activity and disciplined supply commitment, while noting temporary operational disruptions at key mines that did not impact annual guidance.

Brookfield Renewable reported Q2 2026 FFO of $421 million, up 13% year-over-year and $0.62 per unit, up 11%. The company commissioned 1.3 GW, signed PPAs for 2.6 GW, deployed $5 billion, and agreed to $2.2 billion in asset sales. Management highlighted the $17.5 billion DOE loan commitment for AP1000 reactors and the Aypa battery storage acquisition, expanding storage pipeline to over 80 GW. Guidance is positive with record first-half results and a strong liquidity position.

BEPC reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with FFO of $421 million, up 13% year-over-year, and per-unit FFO up 11%. The company commissioned 1.3 GW of new capacity and signed PPAs for 2.6 GW. It announced the $3 billion Aypa battery storage acquisition, doubling battery capacity to about 6 GW, and secured up to $17.5 billion in U.S. DOE loan commitments for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors. Management highlighted record capital deployment and recycling, with $5 billion deployed and $2.2 billion in asset sales, and guided to continued growth driven by accelerating electricity demand.

Q2 2026 revenue rose 15% YoY to $20.6M, with gross margin swinging positive to 20% from -8% a year ago. Operating expenses fell 34% to $20.9M, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$9.8M from -$30.6M, and cash burn improved, ending with $502M cash. Management announced a definitive agreement to acquire GeoPura for GBP 275M, projecting 3x revenue growth, 5x value capture, and 10x TAM expansion, while reaffirming profitability by end-2027.

Baytex reported strong Q2 2026 results with production of 71,243 BOE/d, above guidance and up 11% YoY. Adjusted funds flow was CAD 254 million, operating net back rose to CAD 55.33/BOE from CAD 35.36 in Q1, and the company exited with net cash of CAD 566 million. Full-year production guidance was raised to 71,000 BOE/d (from 70,000 midpoint) while capital remained unchanged at CAD 625 million. Buybacks continued aggressively, with 22 million shares repurchased in Q2 and a renewed commitment to CAD 650 million in 2026.

rows.company_name: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. Common Stock
rows.key_quote: BrightSpring reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.9 billion, up 23% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $206 million, up 44% YoY, both ahead of baseline expectations. The company raised its full-year EBITDA contribution from acquired Amedisys/LHC branches to approximately $35 million and expects ~$600 million in operating cash flow for 2026 with leverage below 2x by year-end. Revenue growth was driven by Pharmacy Solutions' specialty and infusion (up 30%) and Provider Services' home healthcare (up 30% overall, 51% for home health), though home and community pharmacy revenue declined 8% due to IRA impact and customer exits.

Buenaventura reported strong Q2 2026 results with revenues up 43% YoY to $529M, EBITDA up 113% to $277M with margins expanding from 35% to 52%, and net income up 165% to $261M. San Gabriel began commercial sales, contributing gold output, while Yumpag received approval to increase throughput by 20%, with expected cost reductions of 15-17%. Management maintains 2026 guidance and plans to reach 70% gold recovery at San Gabriel by end of 2026, with the ramp-up completing by mid-2027.

Cboe reported record net revenue of $732 million, up 25% year-over-year, and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.56, up 45%. Derivatives net revenue rose 30% to $413 million, driven by record index options volume, with SPX options up 40% and SPX 0DTE up 32%. Data Vantage grew 15% and cash/spot markets rose 22%. Adjusted operating EBITDA margin expanded 6.4 points to 72.2%.

Imperial Oil reported Q2 2026 net income of CAD 2.19B, up CAD 1.241B year-over-year, driven by higher commodity prices. Cash flows from operating activities reached CAD 2.7B. Upstream production of 414,000 boe/d was down 5,000 boe/d sequentially due to turnarounds and weather, with full-year production guided to the low end of the range. Downstream throughput guidance was lowered by about 6% due to unplanned downtime, renewable diesel prioritization, and rail congestion. The company plans to accelerate NCIB repurchases to complete by year-end and continues to see strong long-term growth potential.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Project backlog reached a record $8.1 billion after securing a new $1 billion electronics win in the US.
2. Electronics end market grew 18% YoY, driven by project start-ups and higher demand tied to AI hardware.
3. US manufacturing recovery is driving volume, with double-digit growth in hardgoods sales signaling positive momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Operating margin declined 30 bps YoY (ex-passthrough), primarily driven by underperformance in the U.S. homecare business.
2. The U.S. homecare (Lincare) business is facing significant headwinds from cost inflation and policy changes, prompting a strategic review.
3. Margin was also diluted by a mix shift toward higher sales of lower-margin hardgoods and equipment for electronics customers.
rows.key_quote: Operating margins... declined approximately 30-basis-point year over year. Primarily driven by the Americas segment.

Magna reported strong Q2 2026 results with sales up 3%, adjusted EBIT margin up 70 basis points to 6.2%, adjusted EPS up 29% to $1.86, and free cash flow of $617 million, more than double last year. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for adjusted EBIT margin, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow, and increased North America and Europe production estimates while cutting China. Management noted positive growth over market for the year despite second-half headwinds from program launches and end-of-production, and expressed confidence in re-accelerating growth in 2027.

Quaker Houghton reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $533 million, up 10% YoY, with volumes up 7% and record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $85 million at a 16% margin. Gross margin fell to 35.5% due to raw material inflation from the Middle East conflict, but pricing actions and volume gains offset pressure. The company expects Q3 performance in line with Q2, with full-year adjusted EBITDA growth of mid to high single digits. Key strategic actions include a new China plant startup, a $250 million buyback authorization, and a 4% dividend increase.

Oxford Square Capital reported Q2 2026 NII of $5.1 million ($0.05 per share), up from $4.1 million last quarter, but NAV per share declined to $1.29 from $1.32. Total investment income rose to $9.4 million, and unrealized/realized losses narrowed sharply to $1.1 million. Management highlighted improved loan market conditions, declining default rates, and all CLO equity purchases in the secondary market, but offered no guidance on closing the dividend coverage gap.

Patria reported strong Q2 2026 results with fundraising of $2.3 billion, bringing year-to-date to $4.5 billion, on track to exceed the $7 billion target. Fee-earning AUM grew 32% year-over-year to $48.9 billion, driving FRE up 24% YoY to $57.1 million and Distributable EPS of $0.32, up 31% YoY. Management reaffirmed full-year FRE guidance of $225-245 million but lowered the FRE margin expectation to modestly below the 58-60% target due to acquisitions and investments. Private equity markdowns on older funds were acknowledged but do not affect fees or guidance.

MSA Safety reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $503 million, up 6% reported and 3% organic, with adjusted EPS of $2.40 up 24% YoY. Adjusted operating margin expanded 270 bps to 24.1%, and gross margin rose 290 bps to 49.5%, including about $4 million of tariff refunds. The company reaffirmed mid-single-digit organic growth for 2026 and expects low double-digit total revenue growth, while guiding full-year adjusted gross margin to 47.5%-48.5%, with a moderate tempering in the second half due to delayed inflation from the Middle East conflict. Organic detection sales were flat due to a low single-digit decline in fixed monitoring tied to the Middle East, while industrial PPE grew 16% organically; fire service declined 2% on slower AFG grant orders, but management cited accelerating order momentum and a book-to-bill of approximately 1x, above seasonal trends.

Moderna Q2 2026 revenue was $145M, above guidance, with a net loss of $782M and cash of $6.9B. Management reiterated 2026 revenue growth of up to 10%, lowered cost of sales by $0.1B to $1.7B and R&D by $0.1B to $2.9B, improving cash cost guidance. Flu vaccine mRNA-1010 received unanimous VRBPAC context ahead of August 5 PDUFA, but norovirus vaccine missed early statistical success and will add a fourth cohort.

Pembina reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of CAD 1.064 billion, a 5% increase year-over-year, with earnings up 23% and adjusted earnings up 10%. Management affirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of CAD 4.35-4.55 billion, trending toward the midpoint, and highlighted new assets (RFS IV, Wapiti Expansion) entering service on time and under budget. The quarter saw significant strategic announcements, including the sanctioning of the Heartland Extraction Plant, a positive FID on the Greenlight Electricity Center for Meta, and participation in the West Coast oil pipeline, supporting the targeted 5%-7% CAGR growth through 2030. Guidance was reiterated, not raised, with third quarter expected to be seasonally weaker.

Mettler-Toledo reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $1 billion, up 6% in local currency, above prior guidance of ~3%, with organic growth of 4%. Adjusted EPS was $11.46, up 14% year-over-year. The company raised full-year local currency sales growth guidance to 4%-5% (from ~4%) and adjusted EPS growth to 10%-11% (from 8%-10%). China grew 9%, and emerging markets outside China grew high single digits, contributing to the strength.

PGE reported Q2 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.59 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.64, in line with expectations. Reaffirmed full-year EPS guidance of $3.33-$3.53 and long-term earnings/dividend growth of 5%-7%. Industrial load grew 11.2% YoY; total retail deliveries up 3.9% (2.7% weather-adjusted). New large load tariff approved, raising data center prices ~30% and lowering rates for others; 2027 general rate case filing expected next week, proposing 4.8% overall increase. Progress on renewable RFP and holding company formation; Washington acquisition targeted for mid-2027 closing.

Proto Labs reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $149.3 million, up 10.2% in constant currencies, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.60, a 45% year-over-year increase and the highest since Q3 2020. Gross margin expanded 200 basis points year-over-year to 46.8%, and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 16.8%. The company raised its full-year revenue growth outlook to 8%-10% and provided Q3 revenue guidance of $145-153 million, implying 10% growth at the midpoint. Injection Molding accelerated to 12.9% growth and CNC Machining grew 13.1%, driven by strength in aerospace, defense, data centers, and robotics.

Perimeter Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $105.6 million, up 16% year-over-year, and year-to-date adjusted EBITDA of $146.7 million, up 34%. The fire safety segment grew EBITDA 1% in the quarter, weighed by a federal contract pricing step-down and minimal foam deliveries, but the CFO noted these headwinds ease in Q3. The company closed the acquisition of Monaco Enterprises for about $120 million, a high-margin, military-focused fire detection business. Specialty products faced PDI production issues at a supplier's plant, which the company is addressing with a receiver and plans to reduce reliance.

Pearson reported H1 with group revenue up 4% underlying, adjusted operating profit up 14% to GBP 276 million with 140bps margin expansion to 15.5%, and adjusted EPS up 19% to GBP 0.289. Management reaffirms full-year guidance and proposes a 5% interim dividend increase, with strategic wins including a global certification contract with a leading AI lab and strong Virtual Learning momentum.

Kyivstar reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $339 million, up 19% YoY, and EBITDA of $188 million, up 14%, with digital revenue growing 83% to $74 million. The company raised full-year guidance for the second time this year, now expecting UAH revenue growth of 21%-23% and EBITDA growth of 17%-19%. Mobile customers declined 3% to 21.8 million, but ARPU rose 11% to $3.90 and churn improved to 14.2%. Management highlighted strong cash flow of $104 million, and remains confident in its multiplay and digital strategy despite external volatility.

TransAlta reported Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 291 million and free cash flow of CAD 143 million, with average fleet availability at 90.2%. Results faced softer Alberta spot prices (CAD 29/MWh vs CAD 40/MWh in Q2 2025), but hedging and optimization lifted realized gas prices to CAD 68/MWh, a 134% premium to spot. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance and announced the acquisition of two gas-fired peaking facilities in Colorado for US$1 billion, expected to close in Q4 2026 and add CAD 110 million in annual EBITDA. Positive developments included Alberta data center regulations and progress on Centralia coal-to-gas conversion, while S&P shifted TransAlta's outlook to negative, citing soft market pricing and Centralia's outage.

Alliant Energy reported Q2 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.65, with ongoing earnings driven by higher revenue requirements from capital investments and increased equity earnings from venture funds, partially offset by milder weather and higher O&M expenses. The company reaffirmed its 2026 earnings guidance and is trending in the upper half of the range. Management continues to execute on large load data center agreements, with five signed contracts and a pipeline of 2-4 GW of potential future load. They also reaffirmed long-term EPS growth of 7%+ for 2027-2029 and have raised ~$1.8 billion of the ~$2.4 billion equity needs through 2029.

The Bancorp reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.45, up 14.2% year-over-year, with ROE at 34.7%. Fintech GDV grew 22.5% YoY and fintech revenue grew 21%. The company raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $5.95-$6.05 and reiterated 2027 guidance of $8.10-$8.30. Management expects Cash App to contribute more materially in late Q4/early 2027 and announced two new sponsored lending programs expected within six months.

The St. Joe Company reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $158.9 million, up 23% YoY, and net income of $40.5 million, up 37% YoY, both record highs for the quarter. Gross margins expanded across all segments: residential to 48%, hospitality to 42%, and commercial to 65%. The company allocated $32.7 million to buybacks, $24 million to capex, and repaid $10.9 million in debt, with share count at a 30-year low. Management emphasized long-term capital allocation, continued demand from in-migration, and no near-term constraints from power development.

IRadimed reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $20.5 million, up 0.5% YoY, with GAAP EPS of $0.41 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.46, roughly in line with guidance and reflecting costs from the initial production ramp of the new 3870 MRI IV pump. Bookings more than doubled shipments, with 70% of replacements being higher-ASP four-channel quad systems, and the patient monitor business saw a record 71 domestic units. Management guided Q3 revenue of $23.0-$24.5 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.54-$0.59, and reaffirmed full-year revenue of $91-$96 million; they expect gross margins to recover and reach record levels by Q4.

Invesco Mortgage Capital reported Q2 2026 economic return of 3.8% with monthly dividends of $0.12 per share and book value down 0.6%. Earnings available for distribution fell to $0.50 from $0.55 in Q1. Portfolio grew 12.4% to $8.2 billion, funded via $118 million raised in the quarter. Guidance is cautious: book value down ~2.5% quarter-to-date, spreads widened 7 bps since quarter-end, and management remains hedge-heavy at 97% given uncertainty.

NatWest delivered strong H1 2026 results with income up 5.4% QoQ to GBP 4.4bn, operating profit up 12.4%, and return on tangible equity of 19.7%, which led to upgraded FY26 returns guidance to more than 19%. Customer assets and liabilities grew 13.4% including Evelyn Partners, and the cost-income ratio improved to 46%. Capital generation was strong at 137 bps with CET1 at 13.2%, and management expressed confidence in continued growth and capital generation of more than 240 bps for 2026.

Newell Brands returned to year-over-year net sales growth (+3%) and core sales growth (+2.3%) in Q2 2026, both above the high end of guidance and the first such growth in over four years. Growth was broad-based, with five of six business units growing core sales and the U.S. leading with ~5% net sales growth. Normalized EPS was $0.42, well above prior guidance of $0.16-$0.19, though this included a one-time ~$100 million IEEPA tariff recovery receivable; excluding this, EPS still beat guidance. Management raised the full-year outlook across all key metrics, citing stronger innovation, distribution gains, and improved execution, while noting input cost inflation headwinds and a cautious view on second-half category trends.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI-led innovation strategy is a "game changer," driving double-digit pipeline growth and attracting new customers previously hesitant to leave vendor support.
2. Adjusted revenue (ex-PeopleSoft) grew 10% YoY, and annualized recurring revenue (ex-PeopleSoft) grew 8.1%, indicating strong underlying business acceleration.
3. Confidently reiterated full-year 'Rule of 20' guidance, supported by strong demand signals including a 30% pipe close rate and double-digit new bookings growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Non-GAAP EPS declined to $0.06 from $0.08 in the prior year, reflecting higher investments in sales and marketing for new AI offerings.
2. Billings declined 8.8% year-over-year, attributed to renewal timing, creating noise around near-term growth momentum.
3. Sales and Marketing expense as a percentage of revenue increased to 37.6% (non-GAAP) from 35.5% YoY, pressuring operating margins in the near term.
rows.key_quote: The fact that we are now giving customers a path...has been a game changer...in terms of overall demand generation.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Strong Preneed Sales Growth: Comparable preneed cemetery sales production grew 8% ($29.7M) and preneed funeral sales production grew 7% ($20M).
2) Robust Operating Cash Flow: Adjusted operating cash flow increased 42% YoY to $239M, leading to a $50M increase in full-year cash flow guidance.
3) Improving Funeral Volume Trend: Core funeral volume decline of 1.7% was better than expected, with the trend moderating through the quarter and showing slight growth in June.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Funeral Gross Margin Decline: Funeral gross margin fell 130 basis points to 18.5% due to slow revenue growth and higher recognized watching compensation.
2) Funeral Volume Decline: Comparable core funeral volume declined 1.7% for the quarter, continuing to be a headwind.
3) GAAP Expense Recognition Headwinds: A shift to more insurance-funded preneed contracts resulted in higher upfront recognition of watching compensation, negatively impacting reported funeral margins.
rows.key_quote: Comparable preneed cemetery sales production grew by 8% and comparable preneed funeral sales production grew by 7% for the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. R2 Launch Success: Started R2 deliveries with reservation-to-order conversion rates "meaningfully higher than what we expected" for the premium $58,000 Launch Edition.
2. Raised Guidance: Increased full-year delivery guidance by 3,000 units to 65k-70k and improved adjusted EBITDA loss guidance by $50M at the midpoint.
3. Gross Margin Improvement: Automotive gross loss improved by $299 million year-over-year to a loss of only $36 million, helping drive consolidated gross margin to a positive 11%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. R2 Ramp Costs: The R2 production ramp incurred approximately $100 million in incremental cost of revenue in Q2 and is expected to negatively impact automotive gross profit again in Q3.
2. Macro Headwinds: Management cited increasing costs for commodities, memory, and logistics, as well as macro and geopolitical uncertainty, as creating complexity.
3. Slower Commercial Adoption (Non-Amazon): Adoption of the Electric Delivery Van (EDV) by fleets other than Amazon "has taken longer than we would have expected".
rows.key_quote: That conversion rate from reservation to orders has been meaningfully higher than what we expected, which is a great signal.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Demand stabilization: The underlying book-to-bill ratio surpassed 1.0 for the first time since Q2 2024, signaling a bottom in the market downturn. 2. New growth vectors: Management highlighted a ~$300M long-term annual revenue opportunity in data center applications and secured a EUR 127.4M EU Chips Act grant. 3. Segment strength: Medical revenue surged 39% YoY to $21M and Wide Bandgap revenue grew 34% YoY to $10.6M, showing resilience in key areas.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Core market decline: Automotive revenue fell 19% year-over-year to $116 million due to ongoing inventory normalization across the supply chain. 2. Overall revenue contraction: Total quarterly revenue was down 7% year-over-year to $199.8 million, reflecting broad market softness. 3. Margin pressure from underutilization: Low capacity utilization of 60%, driven by automotive weakness, negatively impacted profitability, resulting in a 16.8% EBITDA margin.
rows.key_quote: Our underlying book-to-bill ratio returned above 1.0 for the first time since Q2 2024, an encouraging sign demand conditions are gradually improving.

rows.positive_highlights: Net profit attributable to shareholders increased 157% to EUR 78 million; The valuation of the concession portfolio grew 16% year-over-year to EUR 4.601 billion; Operating cash flow increased 18% on a comparable basis to EUR 631 million.
rows.negative_highlights: Consolidated net debt increased by EUR 429 million during the first half to EUR 6.788 billion; The Engineering and Infrastructure division's EBITDA grew 4% on 10% revenue growth, indicating margin compression; Working capital saw a cash outflow due to significant costs from bidding on large U.S. infrastructure projects.
rows.key_quote: Concessions continue to account for the vast majority of EBITDA, accounting for more than 91% of the total.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Operational Performance: Achieved record refinery utilization of 102% in a high-margin period and record production in Brazil Upstream. The Pennsylvania Petrochemicals Complex also delivered its best performance to date.
2. Strong Integrated Gas & Trading Results: Successfully offset lost LNG volumes from Qatar with strong performance from its global portfolio (LNG Canada, Nigeria, Trinidad) and significant value capture from LNG trading and optimization activities.
3. Strategic Progress: Advanced its cost-cutting program ($700M delivered in 2026), progressed the value-accretive ARC Resources acquisition, and continued portfolio high-grading, strengthening long-term free cash flow generation.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Middle East Disruptions: Ongoing hostilities caused loss of LNG volumes from Qatar and physical damage to one train at the Pearl GTL facility, which is not expected back online until Q1 2027.
2. Anticipated Q3 Headwinds: Management flagged potential softening, including weakening chemical spreads, more planned refinery turnarounds, and the base oil supply for the lubricants business being challenged by the Pearl GTL outage.
3. Underperforming Low-Carbon Capital: A portion of capital in the low-carbon business is currently unproductive as assets like Holland Hydrogen I are under construction, with returns not expected until 2027 or later.
rows.key_quote: Our refineries achieved a record 102% utilization in a high-margin period.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Broad-based commercial strength: Dupixent global sales grew 38% to $6B, EYLEA HD U.S. sales grew 52% to $596M (exceeding standard EYLEA for the first time), and Libtayo global sales grew 29% to nearly $500M.
2. Sanofi collaboration economics improving: The $3.1B Sanofi development balance is now fully repaid, meaning Regeneron will record its full share of collaboration profits starting Q3, significantly boosting reported revenue from the partnership.
3. Strong EYLEA HD momentum: U.S. physician unit demand for EYLEA HD increased 24% sequentially, and it now comprises ~60% of franchise net sales, demonstrating successful conversion and market share gains.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Standard EYLEA decline: EYLEA U.S. net sales declined 45% YoY to $412M, driven by conversion to EYLEA HD and competition. Management expects sequential quarterly demand declines in the low to mid-teens for the rest of 2026 due to upcoming biosimilar launches.
2. EYLEA HD prefilled syringe delay: The expected approval of the EYLEA HD prefilled syringe by the end of Q2 did not occur, with management now guiding for potential approval "before the end of the year."
3. Manufacturing interruption impact: GAAP gross margin was negatively impacted by unabsorbed costs from a "temporary interruption in bulk manufacturing production" at the Limerick, Ireland facility, though production has since resumed.
rows.key_quote: Dupixent, EYLEA HD and Libtayo all set new all-time highs for quarterly net sales and are carrying strong momentum into the second half.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Reached a decisive agreement with the French state on the Economic Regulation Agreement (ERA) for 2027-2034, providing long-term visibility and supporting an €8.2B investment program.
2. Attributable net income more than tripled to €312M, driven by a €257M gain from the partial monetization of the GMR Airports stake.
3. Implemented cost-saving measures expected to deliver €40-€60M in 2026 to protect margins amid a challenging environment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revised full-year guidance downward, with Paris traffic growth now forecast at only ~0.5% and recurring EBITDA lowered to a range of €2.3B to €2.35B.
2. The operating environment became more challenging due to the indirect effects of the Middle East conflict, which softened demand and suppressed traffic growth.
3. Recurring EBITDA declined by 1% year-over-year, indicating pressure on operational profitability.
rows.key_quote: The Middle East conflict’s indirect consequences have spread more broadly, affecting traffic growth and airline behavior, and ultimately, demand trends.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Ferri and Boot Drive solutions revenue more than doubled sequentially, now representing nearly 30% of total revenue, up from 4% a year ago.
2. Achieved record revenue of $451M, a 127% YoY increase, beating the high end of guidance, with growth across all core markets.
3. Guided Q3 operating margin to expand to 27.5%-28.5% as the new MonTitan enterprise SSD business scales with 5 additional Tier 1 customers in 2H.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Broader consumer markets are challenged; smartphone units are expected to be down 10-15% in 2026 due to rising component costs.
2. NAND supply scarcity is expected to persist until 2028, creating challenges for OEMs and delaying the availability of cost-effective high-capacity QLC SSDs.
3. The transition from PCIe 4 to PCIe 5 in the PC market is proceeding more slowly than anticipated as OEMs prioritize cost-saving measures.
rows.key_quote: Ferri and Boot Drive solutions more than doubled sequentially and represent near 30% of our total revenue, up from 4% a year ago.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. P&C division delivered an exceptionally strong combined ratio of 79.5% for the quarter, driven by benign catastrophe activity and excellent underlying attritional performance. 2. Strong growth in targeted areas, with Alternative Solutions premiums up over 70% YTD and Specialty lines up 19.8% in recent renewals. 3. Balance sheet strengthened, with solvency ratio increasing to 220% and progress made on deleveraging, while also building prudential buffers.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Life & Health insurance service result was reduced to €49 million for the quarter due to a negative one-off arbitration impact of €64 million. 2. P&C reinsurance market is seeing increased competition, particularly in property cat where U.S. prices decreased around 20% in recent renewals. 3. P&C gross written premium was negatively impacted by revisions to prior year estimates from cedents and adverse foreign exchange effects.
rows.key_quote: P&C continued its strong performance...supported by a relatively benign cat activity and an excellent attritional loss ratio, demonstrating the quality of our portfolio.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Significant EPS guidance raise: Full-year guidance was increased to $0.90-$1.10 from $0.70-$1.00, reflecting strong performance and outlook.
2. Strong operating leverage in Truckload: Earnings more than doubled sequentially on only 2% revenue growth, driven by pricing, productivity, and cost cuts.
3. Rapid market improvement: A 'supply-led' recovery with faster-than-expected capacity attrition has created a driver-constrained market with strong pricing momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Driver market constraints: Driver availability is tight, impacting tractor count, creating recruiting/retention challenges, and putting upward pressure on capacity costs.
2. Loss of a major customer: The company anticipates the loss of a large dedicated customer, which will become more evident in H2 2026 results.
3. Intermodal growth constraints: Drayage has become the primary constraint for Intermodal, forcing the company to decline growth that would require expensive third-party capacity.
rows.key_quote: In truckload, we more than doubled earnings sequentially on 2% revenue growth, possible through executing price, productivity, and cost reductions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Revenue Growth & Profitability: Revenue grew 61% YoY to $805M, marking the eighth straight quarter of over 60% growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit 43% and GAAP diluted EPS more than doubled to $1.25.
2. Strong Ad Business Momentum: Ad revenue grew 64%, driven by a 70% YoY increase in active advertisers and 100%+ growth in conversion volume. The automated 'Reddit Max' ad platform saw revenue grow over 150% from Q1.
3. Improving User Quality: Despite search headwinds, new app user retention improved 50% YoY on a relative basis, a key indicator that product improvements are successfully creating more valuable, direct users.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. User Growth Headwinds from Search: Overall DAU growth was hampered by volatile search referral traffic, leading to a slight sequential decline in U.S. DAUs and raising analyst concerns about external dependencies.
2. Inefficient Paid Marketing: Management stated that user acquisition spending "needs stronger attention to improve returns," acknowledging that better user retention is required to justify higher marketing investment.
3. Data Licensing Uncertainty: Management offered no clear visibility on the renewal of major data licensing deals, stating the "range of outcomes is wide," creating uncertainty around a key revenue stream.
rows.key_quote: We turned intent into outcomes with conversion volume growing over 100% and click volume growing over 30% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Secured 6 GW of new large load contracts in Q2, including a 3.2 GW, 25-year deal with OpenAI, bringing the total contracted pipeline to over 17 GW.
2. Data center electricity usage grew 55% year-over-year, driving a 22.8% increase in adjusted EPS and a guidance raise to the top of the full-year range.
3. The prospective pipeline for new large load projects remains above 75 GW, with another 8 GW in late-stage negotiations, indicating massive future capital investment opportunities.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Acknowledged ongoing financing needs to support growth, sourcing an additional $700 million in equity during the quarter to maintain credit metrics.
2. Management noted the presence of 'noise all across the country about data centers', indicating potential political or social headwinds that require proactive communication.
3. The massive 17+ GW load buildout creates significant long-term execution risk related to construction timelines and regulatory approvals for new generation.
rows.key_quote: Data center usage was 55% higher compared to the second quarter of 2025, primarily due to accelerating load ramps from our large load customers.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Core Business Acceleration & Margin Expansion:** Core revenue (ex-divestiture) grew high-single digits, driven by accelerating 1P ARPU growth. Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to expand by ~300 basis points.
2. **Strong AI (MAX) Progress and Monetization Path:** The AI agent MAX is showing tangible ROI in beta (e.g., catching a $290k invoice failure) and is rolling out to all fulfillment customers. A clear monetization strategy is planned for late 2026 via paid autonomous agent bundles.
3. **Strategic Divestiture:** Sold the lower-margin, less strategic 3P revenue recovery business to sharpen focus on the core 1P supplier network, which has better cross-watch opportunities and a cleaner business model.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Sequential Customer Count Decline:** Core 1P customer count declined by approximately 200 sequentially due to the timing of retail enablement programs. Management expects to be flat-to-slightly positive for the full year.
2. **Muted Reported Revenue Growth:** Overall reported revenue growth was 6% and is guided to ~5% for the full year, dampened by the divestiture of the 3P business which reduces H2 revenue by $10.5M.
3. **Slower Analytics Business:** The analytics business, while receiving a platform refresh, grew only about 1% in the first half of the year, with demand still viewed as more discretionary.
rows.key_quote: Core business grew high single digits, driven by accelerating 1P customer ARPU growth from continued upsell and cross-watch momentum.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Brand Momentum: The flagship Steve Madden brand saw a resurgence, with global online searches up 71% and branded wholesale business up 20% in Q2.
2. Significant Margin Expansion: Consolidated gross margin increased 460 bps to 46.5%, driven by higher ASPs, lower promotions, and a reduced mix of private label business.
3. Robust EPS Growth: Diluted EPS more than doubled to $0.44 from $0.20 in the prior-year quarter, significantly beating expectations.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Private Label Weakness: The private label business continues to struggle and is projected to be down mid- to high-teens for the full year.
2. Increased Freight Costs: Management incorporated an additional $0.06 of EPS pressure for the second half due to higher air freight costs to chase best-sellers.
3. International Softness: International comp sales were impacted by conflict in the Middle East, rising only 1% versus a 17% increase in the U.S.
rows.key_quote: Our flagship brand, Steve Madden, was the highlight, continuing to gain momentum as consumers responded enthusiastically to the trend-right assortments.

First Internet Bancorp reported Q2 2026 net income of $2.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share, with total revenue up 23% year-over-year to $41.1 million and pre-provision net revenue up 28% to $15 million. Provision for credit losses declined sequentially to $13.4 million from $16.3 million, while total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million (78 bps of performing loans). Management highlighted a credit inflection point, with SBA charge-offs down nearly 50% sequentially and expectations for continued credit improvement and stronger H2 origination volumes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year ATM revenue growth guidance to 35% due to insatiable AI-driven demand across both LEAP and general packaging, leading to widespread capacity constraints.
2. ATM gross margin expected to exceed the 30% structural ceiling in Q4, signaling a fundamental step-up in profitability and a potential upward revision of long-term targets.
3. Announced plans to double LEAP revenue in 2027 and increased 2026 CapEx by $2B to $10.5B to support a multi-year growth cycle.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Near-term growth is gated by the physical ability to build facilities and install equipment, with the company "just trying to keep up" with demand.
2. Heavy CapEx is causing negative free cash flow, a situation expected to persist "for some time" as the company continues its aggressive investment cycle.
3. EMS business margins declined sequentially due to product mix and higher component costs, with a large portion of its projected 40% Q3 revenue growth being a pass-through of memory price hikes.
rows.key_quote: Hardware infrastructure is a bottleneck. With AI, the hardware requirement is new, insatiable and more complicated and more complex.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong European Performance & Outlook: European segment EBITDA per ton hit a three-year high of $98, with the new TRQ trade tool driving stronger order books and a powerful counter-seasonal Q3 shipment guidance (stable to higher).
2. Confident Guidance & Production Restarts: Management is restarting its full suite of blast furnaces in Europe and guides for sequential improvement in all steel segments in Q3, reflecting high confidence in the market.
3. Clear Strategic Growth Path: A portfolio of strategic growth projects is expected to contribute $1.8 billion in new incremental EBITDA from 2026, with major opportunities being advanced in India, Brazil, and the US.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Rising Carbon Costs: The restart of European blast furnaces will lead to higher carbon costs, which will partially offset profitability gains from higher volumes.
2. Stagnant European Real Demand: Management noted that underlying real demand in Europe is stable but not yet growing; near-term volume gains are from recapturing market share from imports.
3. Liberia Shipment Delays: A heavy rainy season caused delays in shipments from Liberia during Q2, which are now expected to be caught up in Q3.
rows.key_quote: Our European segment delivered an EBITDA per ton of $98, a three-year high, demonstrating the early signs of the improved policy backdrop.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record recruiting pipeline and strong recruited assets of $25 billion, the strongest quarter in nearly two years (ex-large institutional deals).
2. Achieved record adjusted EPS of $5.84 and lowered the full-year Core G&A outlook to $2.14B-$2.165B due to greater efficiency.
3. Commonwealth integration is on track for Q4, with an increased run-rate EBITDA estimate of ~$435 million.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Organic net new assets of $23B represented a 4% annualized growth rate, which is below the company's mid-to-high single-digit target range.
2. The payout rate is expected to increase by approximately 80 basis points in Q3 due to seasonality and advisory pricing reductions.
3. Transaction revenue is forecasted to decline by approximately $5 million in Q3 after reaching record levels in Q2.
rows.key_quote: recruited assets improved to $25 billion... this was our strongest quarter of recruiting in nearly 2 years.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Profitability: Achieved highest-ever quarterly net profit of PLN 1.1 billion and a Return on Tangible Equity of nearly 22%.
2. Strong Volume Growth: Loans grew 13% YoY and deposits grew 21% YoY, outpacing the market. Mortgage sales were particularly strong, up 74% YoY in H1.
3. Improved Full-Year Guidance: Raised 2026 revenue guidance to exceed 2025 levels and lowered cost of risk guidance to ~55 basis points due to strong credit quality.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Margin Compression: Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined to 3.47% in Q2, reflecting the lower interest rate environment, though it is expected to stabilize.
2. Corporate Lending Spreads: Management acknowledged that spreads in the corporate lending segment have compressed, though they see signs of bottoming out.
3. Increased Operating Costs: Underlying costs rose 8% quarter-on-quarter, driven by strategic investments in IT, marketing, and seasonal factors.
rows.key_quote: NII rose by around 3% quarter-on-quarter, supported by loan growth and disciplined deposit pricing.

Ranpak reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency (14% reported), with automation revenue surging 139% year-over-year constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.9% constant currency to $19.1 million, with gross margin up 150 bps year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year automation revenue target of ~$60 million and automation adjusted EBITDA breakeven by year-end, while noting macro uncertainty and a temporary European surcharge to offset input costs.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Achieved the strongest quarterly organic growth in three years at 9%, driven by broad-based performance and a 15% rebound in the OEM business. 2. Non-GAAP EPS grew 18% YoY, and non-GAAP operating margin expanded 142 bps to 22.6%, exceeding the high end of guidance even after excluding a tariff refund benefit. 3. Recent acquisitions like Biolife are outperforming, with its full-year revenue forecast raised to ~$23 million from an original $18-20 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Renal Therapies sales declined 2% due to a product recall, though the issue has been resolved and sales would have grown ~10% otherwise. 2. Ongoing tariff uncertainty remains a headwind, with a projected $16 million impact for the full year, contributing to a wider-than-usual Q3 guidance range. 3. Procedural Solutions sales declined 12% on a reported basis, a headwind entirely attributable to the prior divestiture of the DualCap product line.
rows.key_quote: The beat was broad-based... when our index-style portfolio is all hitting, you get these types of growth rates.

Republic Airways reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $41 million ($0.89 per diluted share) on revenue of approximately $571 million, up 8% sequentially as block hour production rose 7%. The company raised full-year guidance: block hours to ~880,000 (from at least 865,000), revenue to >$2.1 billion (from >$2 billion), and adjusted EBITDAR to $395-$405 million (from >$380 million). July weather has hurt completion factor to 91%, but management remains confident, citing strong partner demand and ahead-of-schedule Mesa integration. Integration benefits are expected to materialize in late 2027 into 2028.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record revenue of $981M (+48% YoY) driven by a 45% sequential surge in the Enterprise Data segment.
2. Raised the full-year growth forecast for the Enterprise Data segment from 85% to 130% due to strong AI-related demand.
3. Strong traction in new product areas, including initial orders for DDR5 memory controllers and sampling 800V data center solutions using proprietary SiC.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management remains cautious on the Consumer end market, which is lagging expectations.
2. The notebook side of the Storage and Compute segment is also an area of caution for the second half.
3. The Industrial segment is 'lagging a little bit' and is considered a 'design win year' rather than a strong revenue growth driver.
rows.key_quote: All end markets grew sequentially with enterprise data growing 45% as we continue to see strong broad based ordering patterns.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Financials: Achieved record total investment income ($149.1M) and net investment income ($92.9M), driven by elevated unscheduled principal repayments of $572.1M. 2. Strong Portfolio Health & Origination: H1 originations hit a record $2.74B, and portfolio companies raised a record $9.3B in new capital year-to-date. 3. Enhanced Balance Sheet: GAAP leverage decreased to 103.9% from 115.4% due to high prepayments, and platform liquidity exceeds $1B, positioning the firm to "play offense."
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Credit Migration: While overall credit was stable, Grade 3 credits increased to 32.7% of the portfolio from 28.6% in Q1, and higher-quality Grade 1/2 credits decreased. 2. Core Yield Moderation: Core investment yield is guided to a slightly lower range of 11.8%-12.0% for Q3 due to portfolio churn replacing higher-yielding paid-off assets. 3. Increased Competition: Management observed that some bank and non-bank lenders are being "very aggressive in terms of deal structures," requiring continued underwriting discipline.
rows.key_quote: Record total investment income was driven by portfolio growth and elevated revenue on unscheduled early principal repayments of $572.1 million.

rows.positive_highlights:
Achieved a nearly 6% year-over-year reduction in direct construction costs per square foot, contributing to a margin beat.
Maintained short cycle times (sub-110 days), enabling a 200% backlog conversion rate and quick response to demand.
Reiterated 5-10% full-year community count growth, which is expected to support second-half closing volumes.
rows.negative_highlights:
Sales orders fell 9% year-over-year due to a 19% decline in absorption pace, reflecting a "softer than normal" market.
Adjusted home closing gross margin declined 280 bps year-over-year to 18.6% from 21.4% due to lower revenue leverage and higher lot costs.
Lowered full-year revenue guidance and guided Q3 gross margin down to "around 18%," indicating ongoing profitability pressure.
rows.key_quote: we also experienced slower than normal watching conditions driving quarterly sales orders of 3.58 thousand which were 9% below prior year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Drilling Activity & Pricing: Rig activity recovered faster than expected, with new contract pricing up 10-15% vs Q1, driven by demand from private E&Ps.
2. Completions Market Tightening: The market for natural gas-powered frac equipment is "effectively fully utilized," leading to meaningful pricing improvements and a strong outlook for further recovery.
3. Drilling Products Record Revenue: Segment achieved its highest quarterly revenue since the Ulterra acquisition despite geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Working Capital Use: Significant use of cash in Q2 due to the rapid ramp-up in activity and a one-time ERP system transition, impacting free cash flow.
2. Colombia Business Exit: Took a $21 million non-cash charge to exit the Contract Drilling business in Colombia due to aging assets and an unfavorable political environment.
3. Middle East Disruption: The Drilling Products segment faced conflict-related disruptions in logistics and activity levels in its largest international region.
rows.key_quote: Private E&Ps have responded more quickly to higher oil prices and are now driving a meaningful increase in drilling activity.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong IAS segment growth: Revenue grew 23% Y/Y, driven by a 40% increase in the business solutions unit. 2. Improved group profitability: Adjusted EBIT increased 18% to €224 million with the margin expanding to 7.7%, aided by efficiency savings. 3. Strategic automation progress: Acquired 70% of Smart Innovation NV to develop autonomous pallet trucks and successfully deployed AI in logistics.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered full-year guidance: Midpoints for revenue and EBIT were reduced due to a weaker outlook for the large ITS segment, citing macro conditions. 2. Weak order intake: Group orders declined 20% Y/Y against a tough comparison, also impacted by Q1 pre-watch effects in the ITS segment. 3. ITS margin pressure: The Industrial Trucks segment's gross margin declined over 100 bps sequentially from Q1 and was also impacted by negative FX.
rows.key_quote: IAS revenue increased by 23% year-over-year due to higher order intake... and driven by a 40% growth in business solutions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record C&I segment revenue of $558M, up 42% YoY, driven by strong demand in data centers and industrial projects.
2. Consolidated gross margin improved to 13.2% from 11.5% YoY, due to better productivity and favorable job closeouts.
3. Record total backlog of $3.16 billion, up 20% YoY, including two new large T&D projects for Xcel Energy valued over $200 million.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Free cash flow was negative $26 million, a significant decline from positive $12 million in the prior year.
2. The negative cash flow was caused by unfavorable timing of tax payments (approx. $30 million higher YoY) and project-related billings.
3. Management guided for a potential headwind to cash flow in H2 as record-low Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) are expected to normalize upwards.
rows.key_quote: The increase in gross margin was primarily due to better-than-anticipated productivity, favorable job closeouts and an increase in scope on certain projects.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Backlog grew to a decade-high of $451 million, supported by a strong 1.2x book-to-bill ratio.
2. Downhole Technologies segment revenue reached its highest level since Q2 2023, while Completion & Production Services revenue grew 13% sequentially.
3. Strategic shift toward long-cycle markets, with over 70% of H1 revenue from offshore/international activity, up from ~50% in 2023.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East contributed to delays in expected drilling and production facility contract awards.
2. Revenue expected in 2026 will be pushed into 2027 due to the contract award delays, tempering the full-year outlook.
3. Downhole Technologies segment margins were pressured by elevated raw material costs for tungsten, explosive powder, and copper.
rows.key_quote: The delay in receiving these awards will push some revenue recognition into 2027 that was originally expected in 2026.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Delivered strong adjusted like-for-like growth of 6.5%, outperforming the global market (4.5%), driven by an innovation strategy that contributed 250 basis points from new products. 2. Exceptional growth in Haircare (+15.6%), Professional Products (+11.6%), and Dermatological Beauty (+10.6%). 3. Impressive acceleration in the SAPMENA-SSA region (+13.8%), powered by standout performances in India (+70%) and Vietnam (+50%).
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported sales were negatively impacted by a -2.8% headwind from foreign exchange rates. 2. The Makeup category grew by only 2.5%, penalized by service level issues in the Americas. 3. The mass market in China turned slightly negative, and the Consumer Products Division's skincare segment has not yet delivered a significant acceleration.
rows.key_quote: The change in sales contribution from new products has been accelerating each semester... to 250 basis points in the first half of 2026.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Resort segment strength: Resort RevPAR increased 12% and hotel EBITDA grew 18.5% with 216 bps of margin expansion, driving portfolio performance. 2. San Francisco market recovery: RevPAR grew 16% and hotel EBITDA increased 24.6%, with 250 bps of margin expansion, continuing its strong rebound. 3. Strong cost control: Total expenses rose only 3.8% on 4.8% revenue growth, leading to a 67 bps portfolio-wide margin expansion to 30.6%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Weakness in specific urban markets: Downtown San Diego RevPAR declined 9.1% and Washington, D.C. RevPAR declined 9.9% due to tough comps and weak government demand. 2. Lagging non-room revenue: Total RevPAR growth of 4.7% trailed RevPAR growth of 6.5%, primarily due to a 20% decline in urban banquet and catering revenue. 3. Overall urban EBITDA decline: Despite strength in SF/LA, total urban hotel EBITDA declined 1% due to weaker convention calendars in other cities.
rows.key_quote: Nearly 3/4 of our RevPAR growth came from rate, a meaningful shift from recent quarters when occupancy gains did most of the work.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong High-Value Segment Performance: The high-value segment drove results, with volumes up 3.5% in H1 and its share of sales increasing to 82%.
2. Stable Profitability Amidst Headwinds: Adjusted EBIT margin was maintained at 16% as efficiency gains (EUR 81M) and positive price/mix (+2.5%) offset negative external impacts.
3. Robust Net Profit Growth: Net profit rose 13% year-on-year to EUR 299 million, benefiting from lower financial expenses and a one-off gain.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Worsening Macro Environment: Management confirmed a deteriorating scenario due to geopolitical tensions, leading to a downward revision of the 2026 car tire market demand outlook.
2. Raw Material Headwind in H2: A positive EUR 32M raw material impact in H1 is expected to reverse to a negative EUR 70M impact in H2.
3. Weakness in Standard Segment: Volumes in the standard segment declined by 11% in Q2 as the company strategically reduced exposure in a highly competitive market.
rows.key_quote: organic growth of 2.5% driven by stronger high-value, accounting now for 82% of group sales and price/mix improvement.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record funds flow ($1.4B) and free funds flow ($925M) driven by high oil prices and production beats. 2. Full-year production guidance raised by 5,000 BOE/d to 385,000 BOE/d with no capex increase. 3. Operating costs fell 13% YoY, with full-year cost guidance reduced by $0.50/BOE, adding ~$70M to free cash flow.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Weak AECO natural gas prices, which averaged only $1.63 per Mcf during the quarter. 2. Management prioritizing debt reduction ($2.5B net debt) over share buybacks in the near-term despite record free cash flow. 3. Planned Q3 downtime of 10,000 BOE/d incorporated into guidance.
rows.key_quote: The combination of crude oil and condensate pricing and continuing to lower operating costs resulted in a robust operating netback of $43.84 per BOE.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Industrial costs improved by over €1.9 billion, driven by manufacturing efficiencies, purchasing savings, and non-repeat of prior year warranty costs. 2. Net revenues grew 13% YoY to €43.5 billion, powered by a 10% increase in shipments. 3. Industrial free cash flow improved by €1 billion YoY to positive €1 billion, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Extremely weak North American profitability, with an AOI margin of only 1.6% despite a 38% YoY increase in shipments. 2. Significant net pricing pressure of negative €456 million, primarily impacting Europe which posted an AOI loss. 3. Total inventory increased 20% YoY to 1.4 million units, reflecting a large build-up at US dealers.
rows.key_quote: The biggest items to improve the AOI in North America are material cost and quality improvement.

rows.positive_highlights:
Exceptional H1 order intake of €12.7 billion, leading to a record backlog of €25 billion, providing strong medium-term visibility.
Diversification strategy paying off with ~75% of awards in the last 24 months originating outside the Middle East, increasing backlog resilience.
Strong balance sheet with record gross cash of €4.8 billion and a net cash position over €900 million, supporting shareholder returns and investment.
rows.negative_highlights:
Project Delivery EBITDA margin fell 350 basis points to 4.3% due to higher costs and logistical challenges from the Middle East conflict.
Full-year Project Delivery margin guidance was lowered to '5% plus' assuming difficult operating conditions persist for the rest of the year.
First-half group recurring EBITDA was down by approximately one-third year-over-year due to the impacts on the Project Delivery segment.
rows.key_quote: EBITDA margins were impacted by operational challenges and higher costs mostly linked to the prolonged conflict in the Middle East.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Financial Performance: The second quarter was the strongest in company history, with adjusted EBITDA over $300M and adjusted net income of $243.7M, driven by record TCE rates.
2. Balance Sheet Transformation: Net debt was reduced by $4.2B since 2021 to reach a $1.3B net cash position, significantly de-risking the company.
3. Strategic Cost Reduction: Refinanced high-cost debt with new convertible bonds yielding ~1%, lowering the daily cash breakeven to a company-low of ~$11,000 per day.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Geopolitical Uncertainty: Management repeatedly cited ongoing conflict and fragility in the Middle East and Red Sea as a source of market volatility and unpredictable risk.
2. Rate Moderation from Peaks: Rates have moderated from the "exceptional levels" and record highs experienced earlier in the year, although they remain strong.
3. Declining Seaborne Volumes: Refined product export volumes declined 11% year-over-year in June, a negative trend that was offset by longer voyage distances.
