rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated gross margin declined 340 basis points to 20.8% due to issues across all segments. 
2. Data Center margins were negatively impacted by 450-550 basis points due to production inefficiencies from supply chain shortages. 
3. Free cash flow was slightly negative, impacted by higher capex and cash payments for restructuring and the pending spin-off.
rows.key_quote: The excess labor along with unfavorable overhead absorption... had a 450 to 550 basis point impact on margins during the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Favorable Loss Development: Realized a $43 million favorable loss reserve development due to better-than-expected cure activity on prior delinquencies, significantly boosting net income. 2. Strong Capital Returns: Repurchased $177 million in stock and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.17/share, signaling strong confidence and returning 124% of net income over the prior four quarters. 3. Expense Guidance Improvement: Lowered the forecast for full-year operating expenses to the low end of the prior $190-$200 million range, indicating successful cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Ongoing Yield Compression: The in-force premium yield continued to decline, reaching 38 basis points, with management expecting this downward trend to persist. 2. Constrained Market Growth: Management highlighted that stretched housing affordability and high interest rates are limiting growth in the overall insurance-in-force portfolio, which grew only 2.6% YoY. 3. Normalizing Credit: The delinquency rate increased 16 basis points year-over-year to 2.37%, reflecting a continued, albeit slow, credit normalization from historical lows.
rows.key_quote: This favorable development primarily reflects better than expected cure activity on delinquency notices received in 2025.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. INGREZZA sales grew 15% YoY to a record $716M, driven by all-time highs in new patient starts, leading to a full-year guidance raise. 2. CRENESSITY sales reached $184M, demonstrating strong launch momentum with its prescriber base nearly tripling YoY. 3. Total revenue grew nearly 40% YoY, strengthened by the successful acquisition and integration of VYKAT XR, adding a third major growth asset.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. VYKAT XR pro forma sales of $94M were sequentially flat, with growth from new starts being offset by discontinuations from the initial launch bolus. 2. Management faces the strategic challenge of accelerating VYKAT XR's growth trajectory now that it is post-acquisition. 3. Future revenue for INGREZZA faces pressure from IRA price negotiations set to begin in 2029, creating long-term uncertainty.
rows.key_quote: INGREZZA second quarter net sales were $716 million, up 15% YoY, driven by another quarter of record new patient additions and sustained demand.

rows.positive_highlights: Strong office leasing volume of 382,000 sq ft, reaching highest level since Q4 2021; Achieved 20th consecutive quarter of positive mark-to-market spreads on office leases at +17.8%; Commercial portfolio reached 94.9% leased, demonstrating strong demand.
rows.negative_highlights: Observation Deck NOI collapsed to $12.4M vs $24.1M YoY due to a 28.5% visitor decline; Full-year core FFO guidance was lowered significantly by $0.13 per share; Pass program visitor channel, a key source of traffic, saw a 45% year-to-date decline.
rows.key_quote: From 2024 year-to-date to 2026 year-to-date, we have seen a 45% decline in pass program visitors.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Remaining Performance Obligations (RPOs) of $17.14 billion, up 44% year-over-year, with 95% of the growth being organic, providing strong revenue visibility.
2. Exceptional performance in Electrical Construction, which grew revenue 24% while expanding operating margin by 210 basis points to an impressive 13.9%.
3. Consolidated revenue grew 19.8% (19.6% organically), driving a 35% increase in diluted EPS to a record $9.06 for the quarter.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Mechanical Construction operating margin declined 110 basis points to 12.5% due to a project mix shift towards lower-margin GMP and prime contractor roles.
2. Management expects a weaker-than-normal turnaround season for the Industrial Services segment in H2 2026 due to geopolitical factors requiring refiners to remain online.
3. Five newly announced acquisitions are expected to have a limited near-term EPS contribution due to acquisition-related intangible and backlog amortization.
rows.key_quote: Electrical Construction generated revenue growth of 24% year-over-year, while delivering an impressive operating margin of 13.9%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Rio Grande LNG Phase 1 construction is ahead of schedule, with Trains 1 and 2 now 74% complete and over 6,000 workers on-site, de-risking the path to first LNG in H1 2027.
2. Successfully refinanced ~$4.6 billion of project debt via a heavily oversubscribed $3.5B notes offering and a $1B term loan, improving the debt maturity profile and freeing up bank capacity for future expansion.
3. Gained clarity on the Train 6 expansion timeline with FERC setting a June 2027 date for the final Environmental Impact Statement, supporting a Final Investment Decision (FID) in H2 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Analyst raised concerns about labor competition on the US Gulf Coast, but management stated this is not an issue for its Rio Grande Valley site due to a unique local labor pool.
2. The company is taking delivery of LNG vessel charters ahead of first production, creating a timing mismatch, but is managing this by sub-chartering vessels.
3. The company has no significant negative operational or financial highlights to report; all construction progress was reported as on-budget and ahead of schedule.
rows.key_quote: The ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz has taken almost 20% of the world's LNG supply off the market.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong YTD financial performance driven by regulatory decisions and lower interest expense, leading to reaffirmation of 2026 EPS guidance ($5.90-$6.20) and long-term 5-7% growth.
2. Significant wildfire mitigation progress, with ~90% of distribution lines in high-risk areas hardened, including nearly 7,200 miles of covered conductor.
3. Successfully completed a ~$2B Woolsey Fire cost recovery securitization and crossed the $1B threshold in Eaton Fire payments to access the state Wildfire Fund.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Massive uncertainty surrounding California legislative wildfire reform, which could lead to credit downgrades (utility is at BBB-) and significantly increase financing costs.
2. Inability to estimate a low-end for total Eaton Fire liability due to the high volume of potential claims (30,000+ in litigation) despite making over $775M in settlement offers.
3. Rating agencies have flagged that wildfire risks are increasingly impacting the broader California economy, complicating the political path to a favorable legislative solution.
rows.key_quote: A framework without sufficient predictability will increase Edison's financing costs, making SCE's investments for customers more expensive.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded over 600 basis points to 36.6%, driven by pricing, favorable mix, and operational execution.
2. The Performance Materials segment delivered exceptional 53.6% EBITDA margins, benefiting from a structural shift to higher-value carbon solutions for hybrid vehicles.
3. Full-year adjusted EBITDA and EPS guidance was raised, reflecting strong first-half performance and management's confidence in durable earnings power.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The outlook for the second half is weaker due to expectations of lower auto production and planned maintenance outages in the Performance Materials segment.
2. The Pavement Technologies segment faced headwinds from high asphalt prices, which caused project delays in international markets like China and South America.
3. Reported sales declined 5% year-over-year due to the divestiture of the Road Markings product line.
rows.key_quote: We benefit from a structural shift to hybrid vehicles, which require our most advanced carbon solutions and contribute a higher-value product mix.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Financials: Achieved record revenue of $187.9M (+8.1% YoY), record net income of $106M (+10% YoY), and record adjusted EPS of $1.38 (+14% YoY).
2. Portfolio Growth: Grew primary insurance in force to a record $227.1 billion, fueled by $16 billion in New Insurance Written (NIW) for the quarter.
3. Strong Credit Performance: Claims expense was low at $13.1M, and management cited favorable development due to a constructive macro environment, a strong labor market, and high borrower equity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Anticipated Seasonal Default Increase: Management expects the default population to 'trend a bit higher' in the second half of 2026 due to normal seasonal patterns.
2. Regional Housing Weakness: Acknowledged 'degrees of pressure' in markets like Florida, Texas, and the Sun Belt, where housing inventories are building.
3. Slight Persistency Decline: 12-month persistency decreased slightly to 81.4% from 82.2% in the prior quarter.
rows.key_quote: We generated $16 billion of NIW volume, ending the period with a record $227.1 billion of high-quality, high-performing primary insurance in force.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong EPS Growth: Non-GAAP EPS grew 25% to $0.50, primarily driven by improved margin from new rates implemented in Montana. 2. Merger Progress: Secured key regulatory approvals from FERC, Nebraska, and South Dakota for the Black Hills merger, with a final Montana decision expected in Q4 2026. 3. Data Center Advancement: Expects to sign Energy Service Agreements (ESAs) with two of three key data center developers by year-end, progressing a major growth opportunity.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Unrecovered Colstrip Costs: Incurred a $0.12 per share negative impact from operating expenses for the incremental Colstrip ownership, which are not currently recovered in rates. 2. Data Center Siting Challenges: One of three prospective data center projects is delayed due to land procurement issues, and management acknowledged local community pushback. 3. Rate Case Uncertainty: The company is still awaiting a motion for reconsideration on its 2024 rate review and will need to file a new rate case to recover Colstrip costs.
rows.key_quote: ...noting that was really driven off of improved base rate recovery versus last year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Q2 results with 8% organic sales growth and 19% adjusted EPS growth, significantly boosted by an estimated $0.25 EPS benefit from customer pre-buys. 2. Solutions Group adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps year-over-year, driven by productivity initiatives and strong low-double-digit growth in the Embelex platform. 3. Company generated robust adjusted free cash flow of $365 million and returned over $210 million to shareholders via dividends and accelerated share repurchases.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. A major Q2 customer inventory stocking cycle is expected to reverse, creating a significant ~$0.50 sequential EPS headwind from Q2 to Q3. 2. Intelligent Labels platform growth was modest at low-single-digits, dragged down by double-digit declines in the logistics segment due to lapping tough prior-year comparisons. 3. Full-year organic growth guidance of 3-4% implies a significant slowdown in H2 as the inventory destocking impacts results.
rows.key_quote: We estimate that roughly half of the organic growth was from customer pre-watch activity.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong organic growth of 4.7%, the best in two years, driven by outperformance in the U.S., Italy, Spain, Australia, and China.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved by 90 bps to 25.8%, with all three regions contributing significantly due to operating leverage and the Fit4Growth program.
Adjusted free cash flow surged by approximately 70% in H1 vs. the prior year, driven by higher profitability and lower Net CapEx.
rows.negative_highlights:
The Fit4Growth program had a negative impact on revenue growth of -3.5% due to store closures and the termination of a managed care agreement.
The U.S. insurance channel remains soft, declining by approximately 4%, which partially offset strong growth in the private pay segment.
The French market is normalizing with lower growth after annualizing the strong performance from the prior year's regulatory reform.
rows.key_quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin... increased by 90 basis points versus last year, driven by operating leverage and the continued execution of our Fit4Growth program.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Shipbuilding Revenue Growth & Guidance Raise: Shipbuilding sales grew 15.7% YoY, leading to a raise in full-year revenue guidance to $10.2-$10.4 billion.
2. Major Submarine Contract Wins: Secured approximately $25 billion in contracts for Virginia Class Block VI and Columbia submarine programs, ensuring long-term stability.
3. Operational Throughput Improvement: Achieved a 12% improvement in shipbuilding throughput year-to-date, on track to meet the full-year goal of 15%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Mission Technologies Revenue Decline: The segment's revenue decreased 3.9% YoY to $760 million, though this was against a tough prior-year comp.
2. Negative Free Cash Flow: Reported negative free cash flow of -$150 million ($31M used in ops + $119M capex) due to timing of receipts, though full-year guidance was reiterated.
3. Slow Hiring Start at Ingalls: Ingalls shipyard experienced a slow start to the year in labor growth and hiring, though trends are now positive post-union agreement.
rows.key_quote: our second quarter results which reflect our continued focus and progress on increasing throughput.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record EBITDA: Achieved a record $2.8 billion in EBITDA, a 17% year-over-year increase, driven by strong global demand and market volatility.
Exceptional Volume Growth: Total pipeline volumes grew 8% and marine terminal volumes surged 33% year-over-year, handling a record 14.7 million barrels per day.
Significant Growth Project Sanctions: Approved construction of two new Permian gas processing plants (11 & 13) and a new NGL fractionator (Frac 15) to support future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
Potential LPG Export Oversupply: Management acknowledged new market capacity could lead to "lower rates than we've seen in the last couple of years" for LPG exports.
ATEX Pipeline Rate Reset: Confirmed that existing tariffs on the ATEX pipeline are uneconomic and that "some degree of a rate reset" is required in shipper negotiations.
Increased 2026 CapEx Guidance: Raised 2026 growth capital expenditure guidance by over $700 million to a net range of $2.9-$3.4 billion to fund newly sanctioned projects.
rows.key_quote: During April and May, we saw an acute global demand for U.S. energy... for the quarter, it resulted in around $200 million.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Screening (Shield) revenue surged to $53M (from $15M YoY) on 66k tests, driven by strong commercial momentum. 2. Secured a landmark coverage decision for Shield from UnitedHealth Group, providing access to ~70 million commercial lives. 3. Oncology test volume grew an accelerated 63% YoY, led by >100% growth in Reveal MRD tests and >30% growth in Guardant360 Liquid.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Full-year free cash flow burn guidance was increased by $10M to a range of $195M-$205M to fund accelerated lab capacity investment. 2. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to $56M from $52M YoY due to heavy reinvestment in the Shield commercial launch. 3. Biopharma & Data segment grew a modest 9% YoY, lagging the significant acceleration seen in Oncology and Screening.
rows.key_quote: The tremendous 63% growth in Oncology volume represented another quarter of acceleration, reflecting the increasing strength of our portfolio.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Net revenue grew 12% driven by strong demand for user research studies related to AI-enabled product development.
2. A large user research study significantly outperformed, contributing 4% of net revenues versus an expected 2%.
3. Raised full-year guidance for net revenue growth to 9%-10% and EBITDA margin to 27.8%-28.1%, signaling strong confidence.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. G&A expenses increased 20% year-over-year due to higher travel, recruiting, and business development activities.
2. Interest income decreased due to lower cash balances following significant share repurchases.
3. The expected full-year tax rate is guided to be higher at 28.5% compared to 28.0% in 2025.
rows.key_quote: Our proactive work experienced strong growth led by demand for user research studies as clients accelerate the development of AI-enabled products.

rows.positive_highlights: AI revenue grew 54.6% YoY, reaching 30.7% of total company revenue. The TMT vertical expanded 36.4% YoY, driven by vendor consolidation at key technology clients. Non-GAAP gross margin improved by 220 basis points to 36.9% due to operating leverage and efficiency.
rows.negative_highlights: Total headcount declined 3.5% year-over-year, from 5,013 to 4,838, primarily from rationalizing non-billable roles. The Retail vertical was flat year-over-year, indicating stagnation in a major segment. The non-AI portion of the business experienced an implied decline as AI growth significantly outpaced total company growth.
rows.key_quote: AI revenue reached 30.7% of the total company revenue in the second quarter, growing 54.6% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Q2 Performance: Achieved record Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.90 and record recurring revenues of $1.4 billion (up 8%).
2. Strategic Acquisition: Announced a $5.7B agreement to acquire MarketAxess, aiming to create an integrated global fixed income network from retail to institutional clients.
3. Strong Segment Growth & Raised Guidance: The rates business grew 24%; FIDS recurring revenue guidance was raised to 7-8% from mid-single-digits due to strong data demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Expense & CapEx: Full-year adjusted operating expense guidance was raised to fund growth initiatives, and 2026 CapEx guidance was increased to $850 million.
2. Temporary Leverage Increase: The all-cash MarketAxess acquisition is expected to temporarily increase gross leverage to approximately 3.4x pro forma EBITDA post-close.
3. Softer Energy Volumes: Energy volumes were softer compared to the prior year's highly volatile quarter, though management emphasized strong underlying structural open interest growth.
rows.key_quote: Our rates business once again delivered exceptional performance, growing 24% versus the year-ago period, as investors... actively manage their duration exposure.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Completed a $600M sale of a 27% stake in its Pinnacle midstream unit, validating the Western Haynesville asset and significantly strengthening the balance sheet. 2. Strong well performance with 11 Western Haynesville wells and 22 Legacy Haynesville wells both averaging an initial production rate of 31 MMcfe/d. 3. Production increased 16% sequentially from Q1, while unit operating costs improved by $0.16/Mcfe, driving EBITDAX margin to 74%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lower natural gas prices were the primary driver of weak financial results, with a pre-hedge realized price of only $2.54. 2. Western Haynesville drilling costs rose 13% per foot in Q2 due to steering difficulties, and completion costs increased 5% due to higher proppant loading. 3. Overall leverage remains elevated at 3.0x, though the balance sheet has been substantially de-risked by the Pinnacle transaction.
rows.key_quote: Eleven Western Haynesville wells turned to sales so far in 2026... with a per well initial production rate of 31 million cubic feet per day.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Reduced SG&A by $26.6M and initiated a new plan for $100M in incremental annualized savings. 2. Grew same-store used vehicle unit sales by over 5%, gaining market share. 3. Expanded Good Sam services and plans gross margin to 61.8% from 59.5% a year ago.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance significantly to $230M-$270M due to market weakness. 2. New vehicle gross margin compressed to 10.9% from 13.8% and used vehicle margin fell to 16.5% from 20.5% due to aggressive inventory clearing. 3. New RV retail market weakened, with new retail registrations declining 16% through May and trends remaining soft into July.
rows.key_quote: The new RV market weakened, and we moved through aged inventory. That decision pressured vehicle gross profit, but it was the right call.

rows.positive_highlights:
Software solutions sales grew 7.8% to a record $99.4M, led by ActiveDisclosure which grew 29% for the fourth consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth.
Capital markets transactional revenue rebounded strongly, increasing 36% to $47.3M, exceeding expectations due to improved market conditions for IPOs and M&A deals.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded by 170 basis points to a record 36.7%, driven by a favorable sales mix shift to higher-margin software and disciplined cost control.
rows.negative_highlights:
Print and distribution net sales continued their secular decline, falling 15% (approx. $6M) due to reduced demand for printed proxies and reports.
A new proposed SEC rule, Regulation E-Delivery, is expected to further accelerate the industry's migration away from print, potentially materially reducing demand from 2028 onwards.
Arc Suite software growth was modest at 1.8%, a continuation of a slower growth rate outside of periods with major regulatory changes.
rows.key_quote: Our second quarter software solutions net sales growth continues to be led by the performance of ActiveDisclosure, which grew approximately 29% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Commercial Aerospace sales grew 18.3%, driven by rising production rates for the A350, 787, and narrow-body aircraft.
2. Gross margin increased to 26.1% from 22.8% year-over-year due to strong operating leverage from higher volumes.
3. Raised full-year guidance for sales (to $2.025B-$2.125B) and adjusted EPS (to $2.30-$2.40) on strong commercial demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Defense, Space & Other sales decreased 7%, primarily due to the divestiture of an Austrian industrial business.
2. Management guided for a softer second half on margins and EPS due to Q3 seasonality, increased hiring, and line restart costs.
3. Foreign exchange created a 90 basis point headwind to operating margin in the quarter.
rows.key_quote: higher sales volume generated greater operating leverage through improved cost absorption, which resulted in adjusted operating margins of 13.9%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Significant margin expansion, with adjusted EBITDA margin up 250 bps sequentially to 14.3%, driven by improved job mix and operational leverage. 2. Strong growth in Technical Services, particularly ThruTubing Solutions' downhole tools which grew revenues 10% sequentially on technology adoption. 3. Cudd Pressure Control revenue increased 8% sequentially, led by a 14% increase in snubbing and 6% in coiled tubing.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Pintail wireline revenues fell 16% sequentially due to aggressive competitor pricing and customer activity reductions. 2. Pressure pumping revenues declined 1% and management sees no meaningful pricing upside without a significant activity increase. 3. The overall market remains subdued, leading management to be cautious on near-term activity levels and customer investment uncertainty.
rows.key_quote: Our downhole tools business is benefiting from more complex and longer laterals that are well suited for our technology solutions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Q4 revenue guidance of $362M-$392M, representing 23% YoY growth at the midpoint, driven by the video distribution patent program (VDP), auto, and wearables.
2. Significant new licensees for the video distribution program, including Meta and Alibaba, demonstrating strong early traction and momentum for this new revenue stream.
3. Full-year non-GAAP operating margin improvement guidance raised to approx. 100 bps, up from a previous range of 50-100 bps.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported Q3 results were just "within range," with better-than-expected areas offset by deal timing issues and lower foundational audio revenue.
2. PC market revenue is expected to be down low single digits for the full year due to lower unit shipments and recoveries.
3. Management is closely watching rising memory chip costs, which significantly impact the mobile and PC markets and could be an offset to future growth.
rows.key_quote: Q4 guidance reflects a 23% YoY revenue increase, driven by momentum in our video distribution patent program, including a large deal with Meta.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record CAP grew to $7.4 billion, providing strong revenue visibility.
2. Revenue increased 29% to $1.5 billion, driven by 18% organic growth and acquisitions.
3. Data center-related CAP surged from $65 million to $223 million year-over-year, validating the strategic expansion into this market.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Materials segment gross profit margin decreased 800 basis points due to severe weather and quarry development costs.
2. Consolidated gross margin declined year-over-year due to margin compression in the Materials segment.
3. Recorded a non-operating charge of $363 million related to convertible notes settlement and remeasurement.
rows.key_quote: Data center-related CAP is increasing from $65 million 1 year ago to $223 million at the end of the second quarter.
